title.zh: 卷十二 魏書十二 崔毛徐何邢鮑司馬傳
title.en: Volume 12: Book of Wei 12: Biographies of Cui, Mao, Xu, He, Xing, and Sima
title.raw: 卷十二 魏書十二 崔毛徐何邢鮑司馬傳 Volume 12: Book of Wei 12: Biographies of Cui, Mao, Xu, He, Xing, and Sima

sentences.zh: 崔琰字季珪，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Yan, courtesy name Jigui, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan, courtesy name Jigui, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 少樸訥，好擊劍，尚武事。

translations.literal: In youth he was plain and slow of speech; he loved fencing and esteemed martial pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was unassuming and taciturn; he delighted in swordplay and leaned toward military affairs.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，鄉移爲正，始感激，讀《論語》、《韓詩》。

translations.literal: At twenty-three the township appointed him village head; only then was he stirred to earnest effort, and he read the Analects and the Han version of the Book of Songs.
translations.idiomatic: When he was twenty-three, his district made him village head; that finally roused him to discipline himself, and he took up the Analects and Han Ying's exposition of the Songs.

sentences.zh: 至年二十九，乃结公孙方等就郑玄受学。

translations.literal: When he reached twenty-nine, he then joined Gongsun Fang and others to study under Zheng Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-nine he formed a party with Gongsun Fang and others and went to study under Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 学未期，徐州黄巾贼攻破北海，玄与门人到不其山避难。

translations.literal: Before a full year of study had passed, the Yellow Turban bandits of Xu Province broke Beihai; Zheng Xuan went with his disciples to Buqi Mountain to escape danger.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet studied a full year when Xu Province's Yellow Turbans stormed Beihai; Zheng Xuan led his students to take refuge on Mount Buqi.

sentences.zh: 时谷籴县乏，玄罢谢诸生。

translations.literal: At that time grain was scarce in the county where provisions were bought; Zheng Xuan dismissed and thanked the students.
translations.idiomatic: Grain ran short in the county market; Zheng Xuan released his pupils and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 琰既受遣，而寇盗充斥，西道不通。

translations.literal: Although Yan had been sent off, bandits swarmed everywhere and the road west was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had been dismissed to leave, but robbers filled the roads and the western route was impassable.

sentences.zh: 于是周旋青、徐、兗、豫之郊，東下壽春，南望江、湖。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved about the borders of Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu, went east down to Shouchun, and gazed south toward the Yangzi and the lakes.
translations.idiomatic: So he wandered along the frontiers of Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu, traveled east to Shouchun, and looked south toward the great river and the lakes.

sentences.zh: 自去家四年乃归，以琴書自娱。

translations.literal: Only after four years away from home did he return, amusing himself with the zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: Four years passed before he came home, finding solace in his qin and his texts.

sentences.zh: 大将军袁绍闻而辟之。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief Yuan Shao heard of him and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The general-in-chief Yuan Shao, hearing of him, offered him appointment.

sentences.zh: 时士卒横暴，掘发丘陇，琰谏曰：“昔孙卿有言：‘士不素教，甲兵不利，虽汤武不能以战胜。

translations.literal: At the time the soldiers were violent and lawless, digging up grave mounds. Yan remonstrated, saying, "Formerly Xun Qing had a saying: 'If soldiers are not trained in advance and weapons are not sharp, even Tang and Wu cannot win in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the soldiers were violent and lawless, digging up grave mounds. Yan remonstrated, saying, "Formerly Xun Qing had a saying: 'If soldiers are not trained in advance and weapons are not sharp, even Tang and Wu cannot win in battle.

sentences.zh: ’今道路暴骨，民未见德，宜敕郡县掩骼埋胔，示憯怛之爱，追文王之仁。”

translations.literal: Now bones lie exposed along the roads, and the people have not yet seen virtue. You should order the commanderies and counties to cover skeletons and bury corpses, show sorrowing love, and pursue the benevolence of King Wen."
translations.idiomatic: Now bones lie exposed along the roads, and the people have not yet seen virtue. You should order the commanderies and counties to cover skeletons and bury corpses, show sorrowing love, and pursue the benevolence of King Wen."

sentences.zh: 绍以爲骑都尉。

translations.literal: Shao appointed him Colonel of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao made him a colonel of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 后绍治兵黎阳，次于延津，琰复谏曰：“天子在许，民望助顺，不如守境述职，以宁区宇。”

translations.literal: Later, when Yuan Shao trained his army at Liyang and camped at Yanjin, Yan again remonstrated, saying, "The Son of Heaven is at Xu, and the hopes of the people assist what is obedient. It would be better to guard your borders and report on your office, thereby pacifying the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yuan Shao trained his army at Liyang and camped at Yanjin, Yan again remonstrated, saying, "The Son of Heaven is at Xu, and the hopes of the people assist what is obedient. It would be better to guard your borders and report on your office, thereby pacifying the realm."

sentences.zh: 绍不听，遂败于官渡。

translations.literal: Shao did not listen and thereafter was defeated at Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao refused to heed him and was routed at Guandu.

sentences.zh: 及绍卒，二子交争，争欲得琰。

translations.literal: When Shao died, his two sons struggled against each other; each strove to win Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Shao's death his sons turned on each other, both eager to secure Yan's service.

sentences.zh: 琰称疾固辞，由是获罪，幽于囹圄，赖阴夔、陳琳营救得免。

translations.literal: Yan pleaded illness and firmly declined; for this he incurred blame, was imprisoned, and only thanks to Yin Kui and Chen Lin pleading for him did he escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed illness and stubbornly refused; they took offense, threw him into jail, and he was spared only because Yin Kui and Chen Lin intervened.

sentences.zh: 太祖破袁氏，领冀州牧，辟琰爲别驾从事，谓琰曰：“昨案户籍，可得三十万众，故爲大州也。”

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor destroyed the Yuan clan, became governor of Ji Province, and summoned Yan as aide-de-camp for the provincial governor, he said to Yan, 'Yesterday I examined the household registers: we can raise three hundred thousand troops—therefore this is a great province.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao broke the Yuans and took charge of Ji Province as its shepherd, he appointed Yan senior clerk and told him he had reviewed the census and this land could field three hundred thousand men—it was truly a mighty province.

sentences.zh: 琰对曰：“今天下分崩，九州幅裂，二袁兄弟亲尋干戈，冀方蒸庶暴骨原野。

translations.literal: Yan answered, "Now the realm has split and collapsed, and the nine provinces are torn apart; the two Yuan brothers have personally taken up arms against each other, and the common people of Ji lie exposed as bones on the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Yan answered, "Now the realm has split and collapsed, and the nine provinces are torn apart; the two Yuan brothers have personally taken up arms against each other, and the common people of Ji lie exposed as bones on the fields.

sentences.zh: 未闻王师仁声先路，存问风俗，救其涂炭，而校计甲兵，唯此爲先，斯岂鄙州士女所望於明公哉！”

translations.literal: We have not heard that the royal army sends the sound of benevolence ahead on the road, preserves and inquires into customs, and rescues the people from mud and ashes; instead, calculating armor and weapons is made the first concern. Is this what the men and women of this humble province expect from you, enlightened lord!"
translations.idiomatic: We have not heard that the royal army sends the sound of benevolence ahead on the road, preserves and inquires into customs, and rescues the people from mud and ashes; instead, calculating armor and weapons is made the first concern. Is this what the men and women of this humble province expect from you, enlightened lord!"

sentences.zh: 太祖改容谢之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor changed expression and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's manner altered and he apologized.

sentences.zh: 于时宾客皆伏失色。

translations.literal: At that time all the guests were awestruck and lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Every guest at the gathering went pale with terror.

sentences.zh: 太祖征并州，留琰傅文帝於鄴。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor campaigned against Bing Province, he left Yan at Ye to tutor Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor campaigned against Bing Province, he left Yan at Ye to tutor Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 世子仍出田猎，变易服乘，志在驱逐。

translations.literal: The heir apparent still went out hunting, altered clothes and mounts, and his aim lay in chasing game.
translations.idiomatic: The heir still rode out to hunt, changing dress and horses, absorbed in the chase.

sentences.zh: 琰書谏曰：

translations.literal: Yan wrote remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan drafted a memorial of remonstrance that opened:

sentences.zh: 盖闻盘于游田，書之所戒，鲁隐观鱼，春秋讥之，此周、孔之格言，二经之明义。

translations.literal: I have heard that addicted roaming in the hunt is what the Documents warn against; Duke Yin of Lu watched fish and the Spring and Autumn mocked him—these are the maxims of Zhou and Kong and the plain teaching of the two classics.
translations.idiomatic: The canon warns against compulsive hunting; the Spring and Autumn ridiculed Duke Yin for watching fishermen—the standards of the Documents and the Annals alike condemn such distraction.

sentences.zh: 殷鉴夏后，詩称不远，子卯不乐，礼以爲忌，此又近者之得失，不可不深察也。

translations.literal: The Yin took warning from the Xia successor; the Songs praise 'not far' to seek models; on the zi and mao days one does not rejoice—the Rites treat them as taboo: these again are the gains and losses close at hand and cannot but be examined deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Shang mirrored Xia's fall; the Songs urge lessons drawn from near precedent; the Rites forbid festivity on ill-omened days—recent examples demand sober reflection.

sentences.zh: 袁族富强，公子宽放，盘游滋侈，义声不闻，哲人君子，俄有色斯之志，熊罴壮士，堕於吞噬之用，固所以拥徒百万，跨有河朔，无所容足也。

translations.literal: The Yuan lineage was rich and strong; their young lord was indulgent; roaming and sport grew ever more extravagant, and no reputation for righteousness was heard. Wise men soon wished to withdraw like the bird that changes color at danger; fierce warriors sank into being fodder for devouring jaws—hence though they massed a million followers and held the north of the Yellow River, they found nowhere their footing could rest.
translations.idiomatic: House Yuan was wealthy and its heir permissive; hunting and pleasure ran to excess and moral renown vanished. Gentlemen of judgment quietly resolved to slip away; bold fighters became prey all the same—so even with hosts beyond count and dominion north of the river, they could not stand secure.

sentences.zh: 今邦國殄瘁，惠康未洽，士女企踵，所思者德。

translations.literal: Now the altars are laid waste and kindly peace has not yet reached everywhere; men and women stand on tiptoe, longing for virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Today the state is exhausted and healing grace has not spread; the people crane their necks, thirsting for moral leadership.

sentences.zh: 况公亲御戎馬，上下劳惨，世子宜遵大路，慎以行正，思经國之高略，内鉴近戒，外扬远节，深惟储副，以身爲宝。

translations.literal: Moreover you personally handle chariot and horse; high and low labor in misery; the heir apparent ought to walk the great highway, act with cautious rectitude, ponder the grand strategy that orders the state, take warning from recent faults within and display lofty restraint abroad, deeply weigh his burden as successor—and treasure his own person as the foundation of all.
translations.idiomatic: You yourself bear the hardships of campaign; the heir should tread the straight path, govern his conduct with care, ponder policies that secure the realm, learn from nearby warnings and reveal steadfast virtue abroad, reflect deeply on his role as crown prince—and guard his own life as the dynasty's chief asset.

sentences.zh: 而猥袭虞旅之贱服，忽驰骛而陵险，志雉兔之小娱，忘社稷之爲重，斯诚有识所以恻心也。

translations.literal: Yet he meanly copies the humble garb of the hunter's retinue, gallops recklessly over perilous ground, cherishes the petty amusement of chasing pheasants and hares, and forgets that the altars weigh more—this truly is why thoughtful men feel their hearts ache.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he affects common huntsmen's dress, races through dangerous ground, cares more for bagging game than for the altars of soil and grain—no wonder those with sense are wounded.

sentences.zh: 唯世子燔翳捐褶，以塞众望，不令老臣获罪於天。

translations.literal: I pray only that the heir will burn his blinds and cast aside his pleated jacket to satisfy the multitude's expectation and keep your aged servant from offending Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I beg the heir to destroy those hunting blinds and abandon his riding coat to answer public hopes and spare this old minister Heaven's reproach.

sentences.zh: 世子报曰：“昨奉嘉命，惠示雅数，欲使燔翳捐褶，翳已坏矣，褶亦去焉。

translations.literal: The heir apparent replied, "Yesterday I received your excellent command, and you kindly showed me your refined points. You wished me to burn the hunting screens and discard the pleated jacket; the screens have already been destroyed, and the jacket has also been put away.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent replied, "Yesterday I received your excellent command, and you kindly showed me your refined points. You wished me to burn the hunting screens and discard the pleated jacket; the screens have already been destroyed, and the jacket has also been put away.

sentences.zh: 后有此比，蒙复诲诸。”

translations.literal: If there are later matters of this kind, may I again receive your instruction."
translations.idiomatic: If there are later matters of this kind, may I again receive your instruction."

sentences.zh: 太祖爲丞相，琰复爲東西曹掾属徵事。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor became chancellor, Yan again served as aide in the eastern and western bureaus with rank as investigating clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao took the chancellorship, Yan again held appointments in the eastern and western bureau staffs as investigating clerk.

sentences.zh: 初授東曹时，教曰：“君有伯夷之风，史鱼之直，贪夫慕名而清，壮士尚称而厉，斯可以率时者已。

translations.literal: When he was first appointed to the eastern bureau, the order said, "You have the manner of Bo Yi and the uprightness of Shi Yu; greedy men admire your reputation and become pure, and strong men esteem your name and are sharpened. This is enough to lead the age.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first appointed to the eastern bureau, the order said, "You have the manner of Bo Yi and the uprightness of Shi Yu; greedy men admire your reputation and become pure, and strong men esteem your name and are sharpened. This is enough to lead the age.

sentences.zh: 故授東曹，往践厥职。”

translations.literal: Therefore I appoint you to the eastern bureau; go and tread your office."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I appoint you to the eastern bureau; go and tread your office."

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，拜尚書。

translations.literal: When the state of Wei was first founded he was appointed minister of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei was first founded he became minister of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 时未立太子，临菑侯植有才而爱。

translations.literal: At that time the heir apparent had not yet been chosen; the marquis of Linzi, Zhi, had talent and was favored.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was still unsettled; Marquis Zhi of Linzi was gifted and the king's favorite.

sentences.zh: 太祖狐疑，以函令密访於外。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor hesitated and sent a sealed letter by box to inquire secretly outside court.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wavered and circulated a sealed inquiry beyond the palace.

sentences.zh: 唯琰露板答曰：“盖闻春秋之义，立子以长，加五官将仁孝聪明，宜承正统。

translations.literal: Only Yan answered on an open board, saying, "I have heard that the meaning of the Spring and Autumn is to establish the son by seniority. Moreover, the General of the Five Offices is humane, filial, intelligent, and enlightened, and should inherit the legitimate line.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yan answered on an open board, saying, "I have heard that the meaning of the Spring and Autumn is to establish the son by seniority. Moreover, the General of the Five Offices is humane, filial, intelligent, and enlightened, and should inherit the legitimate line.

sentences.zh: 琰以死守之。”

translations.literal: I, Yan, will guard this to the death."
translations.idiomatic: I, Yan, will guard this to the death."

sentences.zh: 植，琰之兄女婿也。

translations.literal: Zhi was the husband of Yan's elder brother's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was married to Yan's niece.

sentences.zh: 太祖贵其公亮，喟然叹息，

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor prized his fairness and candor and sighed with deep emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao honored his impartial candor and drew a long sigh.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：植妻衣绣，太祖登台见之，以违制命，还家赐死。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Worldly Tales records: Zhi's wife wore embroidered robes; the Grand Progenitor ascended a tower, saw her, deemed it a breach of regulations, sent her home, and ordered her to die.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Shiyu notes that Cao Zhi's wife wore forbidden embroidery; when Cao Cao sighted her from a tower he judged it contrary to his orders, sent her home, and commanded her death.〉

sentences.zh: 迁中尉。

translations.literal: He was promoted commandant of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commandant of the capital.

sentences.zh: 琰声姿高暢，眉目疏朗，须长四尺，甚有威重，朝士瞻望，而太祖亦敬惮焉。

translations.literal: Yan's voice and bearing were lofty and clear; his brows and eyes open and relaxed; his beard was four chi long and carried great dignity; court gentlemen looked up to him in awe, and the Grand Progenitor likewise respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: His voice rang clear and his bearing was imposing; his features were open and serene and his beard four chi long—awesome in presence. Officials revered him, and Cao Cao too stood in respectful awe.

sentences.zh: 〈先贤行状曰：琰清忠高亮，雅识经远，推方直道，正色於朝。

translations.literal: 〈The Conduct of Earlier Worthies states: Yan was pure, loyal, eminent, and bright; his judgment of classical learning ran deep; he pressed square integrity and straight principle and kept a stern demeanor at court.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xianxian xingzhuang records him as upright, loyal, and lucid, with far-reaching scholarship; he upheld rectitude and wore severity in audience.

sentences.zh: 魏氏初载，委授铨衡，总齐清议，十有馀年。

translations.literal: In the founding years of Wei he was entrusted with the scales of appointment; for more than ten years he unified pure criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wei he held the power to rank officials and for over a decade guided elite opinion.

sentences.zh: 文武群才，多所明拔。

translations.literal: Among civil and military talents many whom he discerned were elevated.
translations.idiomatic: Many whom he singled out among civil and military talent rose to office.

sentences.zh: 朝廷归高，天下称平。〉

translations.literal: The court turned to him as the height of judgment; all under Heaven spoke of fairness.〉
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his standards and the realm called it even-handed.〉

sentences.zh: 琰尝荐钜鹿杨训，虽才好不足，而清贞守道，太祖即礼辟之。

translations.literal: Yan once recommended Yang Xun of Julu; though Xun's talent was not abundant, he was pure, steadfast, and kept to the Way; the Grand Progenitor thereupon honored him with summons.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xun of Julu lacked brilliance but was honest and principled; Yan recommended him and Cao Cao duly summoned him.

sentences.zh: 后太祖爲魏王，训发表称赞功伐，襃述盛德。

translations.literal: Later, when the Grand Progenitor became king of Wei, Xun issued a memorial praising martial achievements and lauding lofty virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Cao Cao became king of Wei, Xun published a memorial extolling his campaigns and virtues.

sentences.zh: 时人或笑训希世浮伪，谓琰爲失所举。

translations.literal: Some at the time mocked Xun for worldly flattery and said Yan had recommended the wrong man.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers sneered at Xun's opportunistic praise and judged Yan's recommendation a mistake.

sentences.zh: 琰从训取表草视之，与训書曰：“省表，事佳耳！

translations.literal: Yan followed Xun, took the draft memorial, looked at it, and wrote to Xun, saying, "I have examined the memorial; the matter is good!
translations.idiomatic: Yan followed Xun, took the draft memorial, looked at it, and wrote to Xun, saying, "I have examined the memorial; the matter is good!

sentences.zh: 时乎时乎，会当有变时。”

translations.literal: The times, the times; surely there will be a time of change."
translations.idiomatic: The times, the times; surely there will be a time of change."

sentences.zh: 琰本意讥論者好谴呵而不尋情理也。

translations.literal: Yan's original intent was to mock those who loved reproof without searching out reason and feeling.
translations.idiomatic: His point was to ridicule critics who carped without weighing circumstance.

sentences.zh: 有白琰此書傲世怨谤者，太祖怒曰：“谚言‘生女耳’，‘耳’非佳語。

translations.literal: Someone reported to the throne that this letter of Yan's showed contempt for the world and slanderous resentment; the Grand Progenitor angrily said, 'The proverb runs 'It is only a girl'—'only' is no kindly word."
translations.idiomatic: An informer called the letter arrogant and slanderous; Cao Cao fumed that the proverb says 'only a daughter'—the word only is already slighting."

sentences.zh: ‘会当有变时’，意指不逊。”

translations.literal: There will surely come a time when things change'—the meaning points to disobedience.'
translations.idiomatic: The phrase about changing times carried an insolent implication.

sentences.zh: 於是罚琰爲徒隶，使人视之，辞色不挠。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan was punished as a convict laborer; men were sent to observe him, yet his words and expression did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was reduced to penal labor; watchers reported that his tone and bearing never broke.

sentences.zh: 太祖令曰：“琰虽见刑，而通宾客，门若市人，对宾客虬须直视，若有所瞋。”

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered, 'Though Yan has suffered punishment, he still traffics with guests; his gate is like a marketplace; facing visitors he strokes his curled beard and stares straight ahead as if harboring resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao declared that though punished, Yan still courted guests like a busy market; he fingered his curling beard and glared at callers as if nursing grievance.

sentences.zh: 遂赐琰死。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan was ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was compelled to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：人得琰書，以裹帻笼，行都道中。

translations.literal: 〈The Brief History of Wei records: Someone obtained Yan's letter, wrapped it around a headcloth cage, and walked with it in the capital streets.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Weilüe adds that someone picked up Yan's letter, wrapped it around a turban frame, and carried it through the capital.

sentences.zh: 时有与琰宿不平者，遥见琰名著帻笼，从而视之，遂白之。

translations.literal: There was one who had long been at odds with Yan; seeing Yan's name on the headcloth cage from afar, he drew near to look and then informed on him.
translations.idiomatic: A longtime enemy spotted Yan's signature on that wrapping, inspected it, and denounced him.

sentences.zh: 太祖以爲琰腹诽心谤，乃收付狱，髡刑输徒。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor believed Yan nursed secret slander at heart and therefore seized him, imprisoned him, shaved him for punishment, and sent him to hard labor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao decided Yan brooded treasonous resentment, jailed him, shaved his head for crime, and sentenced him to convict labor.

sentences.zh: 前所白琰者又复白之云：“琰爲徒，虬须直视，心似不平。”

translations.literal: The earlier informer denounced him again, saying, 'As a convict Yan strokes his beard and stares—his heart seems discontent.
translations.idiomatic: The same accuser added that as a laborer he still stroked his beard and stared straight ahead—clearly he harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 时太祖亦以爲然，遂欲杀之。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand Progenitor likewise thought it so and wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed and resolved to execute him.

sentences.zh: 乃使清公大吏往经营琰，敕吏曰：“三日期消息。”

translations.literal: He therefore sent a senior clerk of integrity to sound Yan out, instructing the clerk, 'Within three days bring me word.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched a trusted senior officer to probe Yan with orders to report within three days.

sentences.zh: 琰不悟，后数日，吏故白琰平安。

translations.literal: Yan did not grasp it; after several days the clerk deliberately reported Yan was safe.
translations.idiomatic: Yan missed the hint; days later the officer falsely reported him calm.

sentences.zh: 公忿然曰：“崔琰必欲使孤行刀锯乎！”

translations.literal: The lord said in wrath, 'Does Cui Yan mean to force me to wield the headsman's blade!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao snapped that Cui Yan must be forcing him to the executioner himself.

sentences.zh: 吏以是教告琰，琰谢吏曰：“我殊不宜，不知公意至此也！”

translations.literal: The clerk relayed this lesson to Yan; Yan thanked the clerk, saying, 'I truly ought not to have done so—I did not realize his intent ran so deep!
translations.idiomatic: The officer relayed the warning; Yan told him he had been wrong and never dreamed Cao Cao would take it that far.

sentences.zh: 遂自杀。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed himself.〉
translations.idiomatic: He then committed suicide.〉

sentences.zh: 始琰与司馬朗善，晋宣王方壮，琰谓朗曰：“子之弟，聪哲明允，刚断英跱，殆非子之所及也。”

translations.literal: In the beginning Yan was friendly with Sima Lang; when Prince Xuan of Jin was still in his prime, Yan said to Lang, 'Your younger brother is perspicacious, trustworthy, resolute, and outstanding—probably not something you can match.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Yan was close to Sima Lang; when Sima Yi was reaching his prime, Yan told Lang that his younger brother was keen, reliable, decisive, and extraordinary—Lang was unlikely to equal him.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：“跱”或作“特”，窃谓“英特”爲是也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi observes: 'Zhì' may also be written 'te'; privately I consider 'yingte' correct.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi remarks that the graph may read te; he believes 'heroically outstanding' fits better.〉

sentences.zh: 朗以爲不然，而琰每秉此論。

translations.literal: Lang thought it was not so, yet Yan always maintained this judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Lang disagreed, but Yan never abandoned that verdict.

sentences.zh: 琰从弟林，少无名望，虽姻族犹多轻之，而琰常曰：“此所谓大器晚成者也，终必远至。”

translations.literal: Yan's younger cousin Lin in youth had no reputation; though kinsmen still mostly slighted him, Yan often said, 'This is what they call a great vessel completed late—ultimately he will go far.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Lin began obscure; even kin looked down on him, yet Yan insisted they say great timber ripens late—he would rise yet.

sentences.zh: 涿郡孙礼、卢毓始入军府，琰又名之曰：“孙疏亮亢烈，刚简能断，卢清警明理，百鍊不消，皆公才也。”

translations.literal: When Sun Li of Zhuojun and Lu Yu first entered the army headquarters, Yan again named them, saying, 'Sun is open, bright, fiery, and stern—firm and terse, able to decide; Lu is clear, vigilant, and masters principle—tempered a hundred times without wearing away: both are talents fit for public service.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Li of Zhuojun and Lu Yu joined headquarters, Yan pronounced Sun forthright and fierce, terse and decisive, and Lu lucid, alert, and principled—steel refined again and again—both statesmen's stuff.

sentences.zh: 后林、礼、毓咸至鼎辅。

translations.literal: Later Lin, Li, and Yu all reached the summit of ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: All three eventually rose to chief ministerial posts.

sentences.zh: 及琰友人公孙方、宋阶早卒，琰抚其遗孤，恩若己子。

translations.literal: When Yan's friends Gongsun Fang and Song Jie died young, Yan nurtured their orphaned children with kindness as if they were his own.
translations.idiomatic: After friends Gongsun Fang and Song Jie died young, he raised their orphans as his own.

sentences.zh: 其鉴识笃义，类皆如此。

translations.literal: His discernment of men and steadfast righteousness were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His eye for character and loyal generosity ran along these lines.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：明帝时，崔林尝与司空陳群共論冀州人士，称琰爲首。

translations.literal: 〈The Brief History of Wei records: Under Emperor Ming, Cui Lin once debated worthy men of Ji Province with Minister of Works Chen Qun and ranked Yan first.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Weilüe records that under Mingdi, Cui Lin debated Ji talent with Chen Qun and placed Yan at the top.

sentences.zh: 群以“智不存身”贬之。

translations.literal: Qun discounted him with 'wisdom did not preserve his person.
translations.idiomatic: Qun dismissed him with the jibe that cleverness did not save his life.

sentences.zh: 林曰：“大丈夫爲有邂逅耳，即如卿诸人，良足贵乎！”〉

translations.literal: Lin said, 'A great man may meet misfortune by chance—yet people like you, are you truly so admirable!
translations.idiomatic: Lin retorted that great men sometimes fall to accident—were men like Qun truly worth more.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖性忌，有所不堪者，鲁国孔融、融字文举。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Progenitor was by nature suspicious. Among those he could not tolerate was Kong Rong of Lu; Rong's courtesy name was Wenju.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Grand Progenitor was by nature suspicious. Among those he could not tolerate was Kong Rong of Lu; Rong's courtesy name was Wenju.

sentences.zh: 《续汉书》曰：融，孔子二十世孙也。

translations.literal: The Xu Han shu says: Rong was a twentieth-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu Han shu says: Rong was a twentieth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 高祖父尚，钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Shang was governor of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Shang was governor of Julu.

sentences.zh: 父宙，太山都尉。

translations.literal: His father Zhou was commandant of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhou was commandant of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 融幼有异才。

translations.literal: From childhood, Rong had extraordinary talent.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood, Rong had extraordinary talent.

sentences.zh: 时河南尹李膺有重名，敕门下简通宾客，非当世英贤及通家子孙弗见也。

translations.literal: At the time Li Ying, intendant of Henan, had a great reputation, and he ordered his gatekeepers to screen visiting guests; unless they were eminent worthies of the age or descendants of families with long-standing ties, he would not see them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Ying, intendant of Henan, had a great reputation, and he ordered his gatekeepers to screen visiting guests; unless they were eminent worthies of the age or descendants of families with long-standing ties, he would not see them.

sentences.zh: 融年十馀岁，欲观其爲人，遂造膺门，语门者曰：『我，李君通家子孙也。』

translations.literal: When Rong was a little over ten, he wished to observe what sort of man Li Ying was, and so he went to Ying's gate and told the gatekeeper, "I am a descendant of a family with long-standing ties to Lord Li."
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was a little over ten, he wished to observe what sort of man Li Ying was, and so he went to Ying's gate and told the gatekeeper, "I am a descendant of a family with long-standing ties to Lord Li."

sentences.zh: 膺见融，问曰：『高明父祖，尝与仆周旋乎？』

translations.literal: Ying saw Rong and asked, "Did your honored fathers and grandfathers ever associate with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Ying saw Rong and asked, "Did your honored fathers and grandfathers ever associate with me?"

sentences.zh: 融曰：『然。先君孔子与君先人李老君，同德比义而相师友，则融与君累世通家也。』

translations.literal: Rong said, "They did. My former lord Confucius and your ancestor Lord Lao Li were alike in virtue and comparable in righteousness, and served as teacher and friend to each other; therefore you and I have had family ties for generations."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "They did. My former lord Confucius and your ancestor Lord Lao Li were alike in virtue and comparable in righteousness, and served as teacher and friend to each other; therefore you and I have had family ties for generations."

sentences.zh: 众坐奇之，佥曰：『异童子也。』

translations.literal: Everyone seated there found this remarkable, and all said, "He is an extraordinary child."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone seated there found this remarkable, and all said, "He is an extraordinary child."

sentences.zh: 太中大夫陈炜后至，同坐以告炜，炜曰：『人小时了了者，大亦未必奇也。』

translations.literal: Grand Master for Palace Leisure Chen Wei arrived later, and those seated with him told Wei about it. Wei said, "Someone clever as a child is not necessarily remarkable when grown."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master for Palace Leisure Chen Wei arrived later, and those seated with him told Wei about it. Wei said, "Someone clever as a child is not necessarily remarkable when grown."

sentences.zh: 融答曰：『即如所言，君之幼时，岂实慧乎！』

translations.literal: Rong answered, "If it is as you say, then when you were young, surely you must have been truly wise!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong answered, "If it is as you say, then when you were young, surely you must have been truly wise!"

sentences.zh: 膺大笑，顾谓曰：『高明长大，必爲伟器。』

translations.literal: Ying laughed loudly, turned to him, and said, "When you grow up, honored sir, you will certainly become a great vessel."
translations.idiomatic: Ying laughed loudly, turned to him, and said, "When you grow up, honored sir, you will certainly become a great vessel."

sentences.zh: 山阳张俭，以中正爲中常侍侯览所忿疾，览爲刊章下州郡捕俭。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian of Shanyang, because as impartial arbiter he was hated by regular palace attendant Hou Lan, was pursued when Lan had a written order issued to the provinces and commanderies for his arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian of Shanyang, because as impartial arbiter he was hated by regular palace attendant Hou Lan, was pursued when Lan had a written order issued to the provinces and commanderies for his arrest.

sentences.zh: 俭与融兄褒有旧，亡投褒。

translations.literal: Jian had an old relationship with Rong's elder brother Bao, and when he fled he went to Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had an old relationship with Rong's elder brother Bao, and when he fled he went to Bao.

sentences.zh: 遇褒出，时融年十六，俭以其少不告也。

translations.literal: He happened to find Bao away; Rong was sixteen at the time, and Jian, because Rong was young, did not tell him.
translations.idiomatic: He happened to find Bao away; Rong was sixteen at the time, and Jian, because Rong was young, did not tell him.

sentences.zh: 融知俭长者，有窘迫色，谓曰：『吾独不能爲君主邪！』

translations.literal: Rong knew Jian was an elder and saw that he had a distressed expression, so he said to him, "Am I alone unable to be a host for you?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong knew Jian was an elder and saw that he had a distressed expression, so he said to him, "Am I alone unable to be a host for you?"

sentences.zh: 因留舍藏之。

translations.literal: He therefore kept Jian in the house and hid him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore kept Jian in the house and hid him.

sentences.zh: 后事泄，国相以下密就掩捕，俭得脱走，登时收融及褒送狱。

translations.literal: Later the matter leaked out; the chancellor and his subordinates secretly came to surround and arrest them. Jian escaped, and they immediately seized Rong and Bao and sent them to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later the matter leaked out; the chancellor and his subordinates secretly came to surround and arrest them. Jian escaped, and they immediately seized Rong and Bao and sent them to prison.

sentences.zh: 融曰：『保纳藏舍者融也，融当坐之。』

translations.literal: Rong said, "The one who received and sheltered him in the house was I, Rong; I should sit for the crime."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "The one who received and sheltered him in the house was I, Rong; I should sit for the crime."

sentences.zh: 褒曰：『彼来求我，罪我之由，非弟之过，我当坐之。』

translations.literal: Bao said, "He came seeking me. The cause of the crime is mine; it is not my younger brother's fault. I should sit for it."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said, "He came seeking me. The cause of the crime is mine; it is not my younger brother's fault. I should sit for it."

sentences.zh: 兄弟争死，郡县疑不能决，乃上谳，诏书令褒坐焉。

translations.literal: The brothers competed to die; the commandery and county were uncertain and could not decide, and so they submitted the case for review. The imperial edict ordered Bao to sit for it.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers competed to die; the commandery and county were uncertain and could not decide, and so they submitted the case for review. The imperial edict ordered Bao to sit for it.

sentences.zh: 融由是名震远近，与平原陶丘洪、陈留边让，并以俊秀，爲后进冠盖。

translations.literal: Because of this, Rong's name shook places near and far. Together with Taoqiu Hong of Pingyuan and Bian Rang of Chenliu, he was, as an outstanding talent, the crown and canopy of the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, Rong's name shook places near and far. Together with Taoqiu Hong of Pingyuan and Bian Rang of Chenliu, he was, as an outstanding talent, the crown and canopy of the younger generation.

sentences.zh: 融持论经理不及让等，而逸才宏博过之。

translations.literal: In maintaining arguments and ordering principles, Rong did not match Rang and the others, but in unrestrained talent and breadth of learning he surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: In maintaining arguments and ordering principles, Rong did not match Rang and the others, but in unrestrained talent and breadth of learning he surpassed them.

sentences.zh: 司徒大将军辟举高第，累迁北军中候、虎贲中郎将、北海相，时年二十八。

translations.literal: The minister over the masses and the grand general summoned and recommended him in the highest grade, and he was repeatedly promoted to central inspector of the northern army, gentleman general of the Tiger Guard, and chancellor of Beihai. He was twenty-eight at the time.
translations.idiomatic: The minister over the masses and the grand general summoned and recommended him in the highest grade, and he was repeatedly promoted to central inspector of the northern army, gentleman general of the Tiger Guard, and chancellor of Beihai. He was twenty-eight at the time.

sentences.zh: 承黄巾残破之后，修复城邑，崇学校，设庠序，举贤才，显儒士。

translations.literal: In the aftermath of the Yellow Turbans' devastation, he repaired cities and settlements, honored schools, established village and district academies, raised up worthies and talents, and gave prominence to Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of the Yellow Turbans' devastation, he repaired cities and settlements, honored schools, established village and district academies, raised up worthies and talents, and gave prominence to Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 以彭璆爲方正，邴原爲有道，王脩爲孝廉。

translations.literal: He made Peng Qiu an upright man, Bing Yuan a man of the Way, and Wang Xiu a filial and incorrupt candidate.
translations.idiomatic: He made Peng Qiu an upright man, Bing Yuan a man of the Way, and Wang Xiu a filial and incorrupt candidate.

sentences.zh: 告高密县爲郑玄特立一乡，名爲郑公乡。

translations.literal: He notified Gaomi County to establish a special township for Zheng Xuan, named Zheng-gong Township.
translations.idiomatic: He notified Gaomi County to establish a special township for Zheng Xuan, named Zheng-gong Township.

sentences.zh: 又国人无后，及四方游士有死亡者，皆爲棺木而殡葬之。

translations.literal: Also, when people of the kingdom without descendants, or traveling scholars from the four quarters, died, he provided coffins and buried them all.
translations.idiomatic: Also, when people of the kingdom without descendants, or traveling scholars from the four quarters, died, he provided coffins and buried them all.

sentences.zh: 郡人甄子然孝行知名，早卒，融恨不及之，乃令配食县社。

translations.literal: The commandery man Zhen Ziran was known for filial conduct and died early; Rong regretted not having reached him and therefore ordered that he share offerings at the county altar.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery man Zhen Ziran was known for filial conduct and died early; Rong regretted not having reached him and therefore ordered that he share offerings at the county altar.

sentences.zh: 其礼贤如此。

translations.literal: Such was the way he honored worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the way he honored worthies.

sentences.zh: 在郡六年，刘备表融领青州刺史。

translations.literal: After he had been in the commandery for six years, Liu Bei memorialized for Rong to hold the office of inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After he had been in the commandery for six years, Liu Bei memorialized for Rong to hold the office of inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 建安元年，征还爲将作大匠，迁少府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jian'an, he was summoned back as grand artisan and then promoted to chamberlain for revenues.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jian'an, he was summoned back as grand artisan and then promoted to chamberlain for revenues.

sentences.zh: 每朝会访对，辄爲议主，诸卿大夫寄名而已。

translations.literal: Whenever there was court assembly, consultation, and response, he became the chief voice in debate; the various ministers and grandees merely lent their names.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was court assembly, consultation, and response, he became the chief voice in debate; the various ministers and grandees merely lent their names.

sentences.zh: 司马彪《九州春秋》曰：融在北海，自以智能优赡，溢才命世，当时豪俊皆不能及。

translations.literal: Sima Biao's Jiuzhou chunqiu says: When Rong was in Beihai, he considered his wisdom and abilities superior and abundant, and his overflowing talent destined for the age; none of the heroes of the time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao's Jiuzhou chunqiu says: When Rong was in Beihai, he considered his wisdom and abilities superior and abundant, and his overflowing talent destined for the age; none of the heroes of the time could match him.

sentences.zh: 亦自许大志，且欲举军曜甲，与群贤要功，自於海岱结殖根本，不肯碌碌如平居郡守，事方伯、赴期会而已。

translations.literal: He also credited himself with great ambition and wished to raise an army and display armor, seek merit with the assembled worthies, and plant foundations for himself between the sea and Mount Dai; he would not be mediocre like an ordinary commandery governor, merely serving provincial chiefs and attending scheduled meetings.
translations.idiomatic: He also credited himself with great ambition and wished to raise an army and display armor, seek merit with the assembled worthies, and plant foundations for himself between the sea and Mount Dai; he would not be mediocre like an ordinary commandery governor, merely serving provincial chiefs and attending scheduled meetings.

sentences.zh: 然其所任用，好奇取异，皆轻剽之才。

translations.literal: Yet those he employed were chosen for novelty and strangeness, and all were frivolous and nimble talents.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those he employed were chosen for novelty and strangeness, and all were frivolous and nimble talents.

sentences.zh: 至於稽古之士，谬爲恭敬，礼之虽备，不与论国事也。

translations.literal: As for scholars who examined antiquity, he mistakenly treated them with reverence; although his courtesy toward them was complete, he did not discuss affairs of state with them.
translations.idiomatic: As for scholars who examined antiquity, he mistakenly treated them with reverence; although his courtesy toward them was complete, he did not discuss affairs of state with them.

sentences.zh: 高密郑玄，称之郑公，执子孙礼。

translations.literal: Toward Zheng Xuan of Gaomi, he called him Lord Zheng and performed the rites of a son or grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Toward Zheng Xuan of Gaomi, he called him Lord Zheng and performed the rites of a son or grandson.

sentences.zh: 及高谈教令，盈溢官曹，辞气温雅，可玩而诵。

translations.literal: When he spoke loftily and issued instructions and orders, they overflowed the offices; their wording and tone were warm and elegant, worthy of admiration and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke loftily and issued instructions and orders, they overflowed the offices; their wording and tone were warm and elegant, worthy of admiration and recitation.

sentences.zh: 论事考实，难可悉行。

translations.literal: But when matters were discussed and tested against reality, they could hardly all be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: But when matters were discussed and tested against reality, they could hardly all be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 但能张磔网罗，其自理甚疏。

translations.literal: He could only spread and stretch the nets; his own ordering was very loose.
translations.idiomatic: He could only spread and stretch the nets; his own ordering was very loose.

sentences.zh: 租赋少稽，一朝杀五部督邮。

translations.literal: When taxes and levies were slightly delayed, he killed five district inspectors in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: When taxes and levies were slightly delayed, he killed five district inspectors in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 奸民污吏，猾乱朝市，亦不能治。

translations.literal: Treacherous people and corrupt officials brought disorder to court and market, and he also could not govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous people and corrupt officials brought disorder to court and market, and he also could not govern them.

sentences.zh: 幽州精兵乱，至徐州，卒到城下，举国皆恐。

translations.literal: When elite troops from You Province mutinied, reached Xu Province, and suddenly arrived below the city walls, the whole kingdom was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When elite troops from You Province mutinied, reached Xu Province, and suddenly arrived below the city walls, the whole kingdom was afraid.

sentences.zh: 融直出说之，令无异志。

translations.literal: Rong went straight out and persuaded them, causing them to have no contrary intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Rong went straight out and persuaded them, causing them to have no contrary intentions.

sentences.zh: 遂与别校谋夜覆幽州，幽州军败，悉有其众。

translations.literal: He then plotted with another colonel to overturn the You men at night; the You army was defeated, and Rong took all their troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted with another colonel to overturn the You men at night; the You army was defeated, and Rong took all their troops.

sentences.zh: 无几时，还复叛亡。

translations.literal: Before long, they rebelled and fled again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, they rebelled and fled again.

sentences.zh: 黄巾将至，融大饮醇酒，躬自上马，御之涞水之上。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans were about to arrive, Rong drank heavily of strong wine, personally mounted his horse, and resisted them on the bank of the Lai River.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans were about to arrive, Rong drank heavily of strong wine, personally mounted his horse, and resisted them on the bank of the Lai River.

sentences.zh: 寇令上部与融相拒，两翼径涉水，直到所治城。

translations.literal: The bandits ordered their upper division to confront Rong, while their two wings crossed straight through the water and went directly to the city where he governed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits ordered their upper division to confront Rong, while their two wings crossed straight through the water and went directly to the city where he governed.

sentences.zh: 城溃，融不得入，转至南县，左右稍叛。

translations.literal: The city collapsed, and Rong could not enter it; he turned to Nan County, and those around him gradually rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The city collapsed, and Rong could not enter it; he turned to Nan County, and those around him gradually rebelled.

sentences.zh: 连年倾覆，事无所济，遂不能保鄣四境，弃郡而去。

translations.literal: After successive years of collapse, nothing was rescued, and so he could not preserve and defend the four borders; he abandoned the commandery and left.
translations.idiomatic: After successive years of collapse, nothing was rescued, and so he could not preserve and defend the four borders; he abandoned the commandery and left.

sentences.zh: 后徙徐州，以北海相自还领青州刺史，治郡北陲。

translations.literal: Later he moved to Xu Province; as chancellor of Beihai, he returned on his own to hold the office of inspector of Qing Province and governed on the northern frontier of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he moved to Xu Province; as chancellor of Beihai, he returned on his own to hold the office of inspector of Qing Province and governed on the northern frontier of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 欲附山东，外接辽东，得戎马之利，建树根本，孤立一隅，不与共也。

translations.literal: He wished to attach himself to Shandong, connect externally with Liaodong, obtain the benefit of horses and arms, establish a foundation, and stand alone in one corner rather than join with others.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to attach himself to Shandong, connect externally with Liaodong, obtain the benefit of horses and arms, establish a foundation, and stand alone in one corner rather than join with others.

sentences.zh: 于时曹、袁、公孙共相首尾，战士不满数百，谷不至万斛。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Cao, Yuan Shao, and Gongsun Zan were linked head and tail with one another; Rong's fighting men did not amount to several hundred, and his grain did not reach ten thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cao Cao, Yuan Shao, and Gongsun Zan were linked head and tail with one another; Rong's fighting men did not amount to several hundred, and his grain did not reach ten thousand hu.

sentences.zh: 王子法、刘孔慈凶辩小才，信爲腹心。

translations.literal: Wang Zifa and Liu Kongci were fierce, argumentative minor talents, and he trusted them as intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zifa and Liu Kongci were fierce, argumentative minor talents, and he trusted them as intimates.

sentences.zh: 左丞祖、刘义逊清隽之士，备在坐席而已，言此民望，不可失也。

translations.literal: Zuo Chengzu and Liu Yixun were pure and refined men, but they were merely present among those seated; people said these were men of public reputation and could not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Chengzu and Liu Yixun were pure and refined men, but they were merely present among those seated; people said these were men of public reputation and could not be lost.

sentences.zh: 丞祖劝融自讬强国，融不听而杀之。

translations.literal: Chengzu urged Rong to entrust himself to a strong state; Rong did not listen and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu urged Rong to entrust himself to a strong state; Rong did not listen and killed him.

sentences.zh: 义逊弃去。

translations.literal: Yixun abandoned him and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yixun abandoned him and left.

sentences.zh: 遂爲袁谭所攻，自春至夏，城小寇众，流矢雨集。

translations.literal: He was then attacked by Yuan Tan. From spring to summer, the city was small and the attackers many, and stray arrows gathered like rain.
translations.idiomatic: He was then attacked by Yuan Tan. From spring to summer, the city was small and the attackers many, and stray arrows gathered like rain.

sentences.zh: 然融凭几安坐，读书论议自若。

translations.literal: Yet Rong leaned on his armrest and sat calmly, reading books and discussing matters as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Rong leaned on his armrest and sat calmly, reading books and discussing matters as before.

sentences.zh: 城坏众亡，身奔山东，室家爲谭所虏。

translations.literal: When the city broke and his people fled, he himself fled to Shandong, and his household was captured by Tan.
translations.idiomatic: When the city broke and his people fled, he himself fled to Shandong, and his household was captured by Tan.

sentences.zh: 张璠《汉纪》曰：融在郡八年，仅以身免。

translations.literal: Zhang Fan's Han ji says: Rong was in the commandery for eight years and escaped only with his own person.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan's Han ji says: Rong was in the commandery for eight years and escaped only with his own person.

sentences.zh: 帝初都许，融以爲宜略依旧制，定王畿，正司隶所部爲千里之封，乃引公卿上书言其义。

translations.literal: When the emperor first made his capital at Xu, Rong believed it was appropriate to follow the old system in outline, fix the royal domain, and set the territory administered by the metropolitan commandant as a thousand-li enclosure; he then led the dukes and ministers in submitting a letter explaining its principle.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first made his capital at Xu, Rong believed it was appropriate to follow the old system in outline, fix the royal domain, and set the territory administered by the metropolitan commandant as a thousand-li enclosure; he then led the dukes and ministers in submitting a letter explaining its principle.

sentences.zh: 是时天下草创，曹、袁之权未分，融所建明，不识时务。

translations.literal: At this time all under Heaven was newly forming, and the power of Cao Cao and Yuan Shao had not yet been divided; what Rong established and clarified did not understand the needs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: At this time all under Heaven was newly forming, and the power of Cao Cao and Yuan Shao had not yet been divided; what Rong established and clarified did not understand the needs of the time.

sentences.zh: 又天性气爽，颇推平生之意，狎侮太祖。

translations.literal: Moreover, he was by nature frank in temperament, rather pressed the intentions he had held all his life, and treated Grand Progenitor with familiarity and contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he was by nature frank in temperament, rather pressed the intentions he had held all his life, and treated Grand Progenitor with familiarity and contempt.

sentences.zh: 太祖制酒禁，而融书啁之曰：『天有酒旗之星，地列酒泉之郡，人有旨酒之德，故尧不饮千锺，无以成其圣。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor imposed a prohibition on wine, and Rong wrote to mock him, saying, "In Heaven there is the star of the Wine Banner; on earth there is arrayed the commandery of Wine Spring; among men there is the virtue of fine wine. Therefore, if Yao had not drunk a thousand zhong, he would have had no way to complete his sagehood.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor imposed a prohibition on wine, and Rong wrote to mock him, saying, "In Heaven there is the star of the Wine Banner; on earth there is arrayed the commandery of Wine Spring; among men there is the virtue of fine wine. Therefore, if Yao had not drunk a thousand zhong, he would have had no way to complete his sagehood.

sentences.zh: 且桀纣以色亡国，今令不禁婚姻也。』

translations.literal: Moreover, Jie and Zhou lost their states through sex, yet the present order does not prohibit marriage."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Jie and Zhou lost their states through sex, yet the present order does not prohibit marriage."

sentences.zh: 太祖外虽宽容，而内不能平。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor was outwardly tolerant, but inwardly he could not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor was outwardly tolerant, but inwardly he could not be at peace.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫郗虑知旨，以法免融官。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Xi Lu understood his intent and removed Rong from office by law.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Xi Lu understood his intent and removed Rong from office by law.

sentences.zh: 岁馀，拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Rong was appointed grand master for palace leisure.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, Rong was appointed grand master for palace leisure.

sentences.zh: 虽居家失势，而宾客日满其门，爱才乐酒，常叹曰：『坐上客常满，樽中酒不空，吾无忧矣。』

translations.literal: Although he lived at home and had lost power, guests filled his gate each day. He loved talent and delighted in wine, and he often sighed, "If the guests on the mats are always full and the wine in the cups is not empty, I have no worries."
translations.idiomatic: Although he lived at home and had lost power, guests filled his gate each day. He loved talent and delighted in wine, and he often sighed, "If the guests on the mats are always full and the wine in the cups is not empty, I have no worries."

sentences.zh: 虎贲士有貌似蔡邕者，融每酒酣，辄引与同坐，曰：『虽无老成人，尚有典刑。』

translations.literal: There was a Tiger Guard soldier whose appearance resembled Cai Yong; whenever Rong was merry with wine, he always drew him in to sit with him and said, "Although there is no mature elder, there is still the model form."
translations.idiomatic: There was a Tiger Guard soldier whose appearance resembled Cai Yong; whenever Rong was merry with wine, he always drew him in to sit with him and said, "Although there is no mature elder, there is still the model form."

sentences.zh: 其好士如此。

translations.literal: Such was his fondness for gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his fondness for gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 《续汉书》曰：太尉杨彪与袁术婚姻，术僭号，太祖与彪有隙，因是执彪，将杀焉。

translations.literal: The Xu Han shu says: Grand commandant Yang Biao was connected by marriage with Yuan Shu. When Shu usurped a title, Grand Progenitor had a grudge against Biao and therefore arrested Biao, intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu Han shu says: Grand commandant Yang Biao was connected by marriage with Yuan Shu. When Shu usurped a title, Grand Progenitor had a grudge against Biao and therefore arrested Biao, intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 融闻之，不及朝服，往见太祖曰：『杨公累世清德，四叶重光，周书「父子兄弟，罪不相及」，况以袁氏之罪乎？

translations.literal: Rong heard of this and, not taking time to put on court dress, went to see Grand Progenitor and said, "Lord Yang has had pure virtue for successive generations and four leaves of repeated radiance. The Documents of Zhou says, 'Fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers: guilt does not reach one another.' How much less should this be so for the crime of the Yuan clan?
translations.idiomatic: Rong heard of this and, not taking time to put on court dress, went to see Grand Progenitor and said, "Lord Yang has had pure virtue for successive generations and four leaves of repeated radiance. The Documents of Zhou says, 'Fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers: guilt does not reach one another.' How much less should this be so for the crime of the Yuan clan?

sentences.zh: 易称「积善馀庆」，但欺人耳。』

translations.literal: The Changes says, 'Accumulated goodness leaves surplus blessings.' Is this merely deceiving people?"
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'Accumulated goodness leaves surplus blessings.' Is this merely deceiving people?"

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：『国家之意也。』

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said, "It is the intention of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor said, "It is the intention of the state."

sentences.zh: 融曰：『假使成王欲杀召公，则周公可得言不知邪？

translations.literal: Rong said, "Suppose King Cheng had wished to kill the Duke of Shao; could the Duke of Zhou have been able to say that he did not know?
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Suppose King Cheng had wished to kill the Duke of Shao; could the Duke of Zhou have been able to say that he did not know?

sentences.zh: 今天下缨緌搢绅之士所以瞻仰明公者，以明公聪明仁智，辅相汉朝，举直措枉，致之雍熙耳。

translations.literal: The reason why the capped and sashed gentlemen under Heaven look up to Your Enlightened Lordship is that Your Enlightened Lordship is perceptive, humane, and wise, assists the Han court, raises the straight and sets aside the crooked, and brings it to harmony and brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The reason why the capped and sashed gentlemen under Heaven look up to Your Enlightened Lordship is that Your Enlightened Lordship is perceptive, humane, and wise, assists the Han court, raises the straight and sets aside the crooked, and brings it to harmony and brightness.

sentences.zh: 今横杀无辜，则海内观听，谁不解体？

translations.literal: Now if you recklessly kill the innocent, among all within the seas who sees and hears of it and will not fall apart?
translations.idiomatic: Now if you recklessly kill the innocent, among all within the seas who sees and hears of it and will not fall apart?

sentences.zh: 孔融鲁国男子，明日便当褰衣而去，不复朝矣。』

translations.literal: I, Kong Rong, am a man of Lu; tomorrow I will lift my robes and leave, and will not come to court again."
translations.idiomatic: I, Kong Rong, am a man of Lu; tomorrow I will lift my robes and leave, and will not come to court again."

sentences.zh: 太祖意解，遂理出彪。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor's intent relaxed, and he accordingly reviewed the case and released Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor's intent relaxed, and he accordingly reviewed the case and released Biao.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：袁绍之败也，融与太祖书曰：『武王伐纣，以妲己赐周公。』

translations.literal: The Wei shi chunqiu says: When Yuan Shao was defeated, Rong wrote to Grand Progenitor, saying, "When King Wu attacked Zhou, he bestowed Daji on the Duke of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu says: When Yuan Shao was defeated, Rong wrote to Grand Progenitor, saying, "When King Wu attacked Zhou, he bestowed Daji on the Duke of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 太祖以融学博，谓书传所纪。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor considered Rong learned and broad, and thought this was recorded in the documents and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor considered Rong learned and broad, and thought this was recorded in the documents and commentaries.

sentences.zh: 后见，问之，对曰：『以今度之，想其当然耳！』

translations.literal: Later, when he saw Rong, he asked him about it. Rong replied, "Judging it by the present, I imagined that it must have been so!"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he saw Rong, he asked him about it. Rong replied, "Judging it by the present, I imagined that it must have been so!"

sentences.zh: 十三年，融对孙权使，有讪谤之言，坐弃市。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Rong, when responding to Sun Quan's envoy, had words of ridicule and slander, and for this crime was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Rong, when responding to Sun Quan's envoy, had words of ridicule and slander, and for this crime was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 二子年八岁，时方弈棋，融被收，端坐不起。

translations.literal: His two sons were eight years old. At the time they were playing chess; when Rong was arrested, they sat upright and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons were eight years old. At the time they were playing chess; when Rong was arrested, they sat upright and did not rise.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：『而父见执，不起何也？』

translations.literal: Those nearby said, "Your father is being arrested; why do you not rise?"
translations.idiomatic: Those nearby said, "Your father is being arrested; why do you not rise?"

sentences.zh: 二子曰：『安有巢毁而卵不破者乎！』

translations.literal: The two sons said, "How could there be a nest destroyed and the eggs not broken!"
translations.idiomatic: The two sons said, "How could there be a nest destroyed and the eggs not broken!"

sentences.zh: 遂俱见杀。

translations.literal: They were then both killed.
translations.idiomatic: They were then both killed.

sentences.zh: 融有高名清才，世多哀之。

translations.literal: Rong had a lofty reputation and pure talent, and many in the age pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had a lofty reputation and pure talent, and many in the age pitied him.

sentences.zh: 太祖惧远近之议也，乃令曰：『太中大夫孔融既伏其罪矣，然世人多采其虚名，少於核实，见融浮艳，好作变异，眩其诳诈，不复察其乱俗也。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor feared criticism from near and far and therefore issued an order, saying, "Grand master for palace leisure Kong Rong has already submitted to his crime, yet people of the age often take up his empty reputation and are sparse in examining the facts. Seeing Rong's superficial brilliance and his fondness for producing strange novelties, they are dazzled by his deception and no longer examine how he disordered custom.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor feared criticism from near and far and therefore issued an order, saying, "Grand master for palace leisure Kong Rong has already submitted to his crime, yet people of the age often take up his empty reputation and are sparse in examining the facts. Seeing Rong's superficial brilliance and his fondness for producing strange novelties, they are dazzled by his deception and no longer examine how he disordered custom.

sentences.zh: 此州人说平原祢衡受传融论，以爲父母与人无亲，譬若鲊器，寄盛其中，又言若遭饥馑，而父不肖，宁赡活馀人。

translations.literal: A man of this province says that Mi Heng of Pingyuan received and transmitted Rong's argument, taking it that parents have no kinship with a person, but are like a vessel for salted fish in which one is temporarily contained; he also said that if famine were encountered and one's father were unworthy, one should rather support and keep alive someone else.
translations.idiomatic: A man of this province says that Mi Heng of Pingyuan received and transmitted Rong's argument, taking it that parents have no kinship with a person, but are like a vessel for salted fish in which one is temporarily contained; he also said that if famine were encountered and one's father were unworthy, one should rather support and keep alive someone else.

sentences.zh: 融违天反道，败伦乱理，虽肆市朝，犹恨其晚。

translations.literal: Rong violated Heaven and rebelled against the Way, ruined the relationships and disordered principle. Though he was exposed in the marketplace and court, I still regret that it was late.
translations.idiomatic: Rong violated Heaven and rebelled against the Way, ruined the relationships and disordered principle. Though he was exposed in the marketplace and court, I still regret that it was late.

sentences.zh: 更以此事列上，宣示诸军将校掾属，皆使闻见。』

translations.literal: Again list this matter above and proclaim it to the generals, colonels, assistants, and staff of the armies, making all hear and see it."
translations.idiomatic: Again list this matter above and proclaim it to the generals, colonels, assistants, and staff of the armies, making all hear and see it."

sentences.zh: 《世语》曰：融二子，皆龆龀。

translations.literal: The Shiyu says: Rong's two sons were both at the age of shedding milk teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says: Rong's two sons were both at the age of shedding milk teeth.

sentences.zh: 融见收，顾谓二子曰：『何以不辞？』

translations.literal: When Rong was arrested, he looked back and said to his two sons, "Why do you not take leave?"
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was arrested, he looked back and said to his two sons, "Why do you not take leave?"

sentences.zh: 二子俱曰：『父尚如此，复何所辞！』

translations.literal: The two sons both said, "When Father is already like this, what further leave-taking is there!"
translations.idiomatic: The two sons both said, "When Father is already like this, what further leave-taking is there!"

sentences.zh: 以爲必俱死也。

translations.literal: They thought that they would certainly all die together.
translations.idiomatic: They thought that they would certainly all die together.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以爲《世语》云融二子不辞，知必俱死，犹差可安。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi believes: The Shiyu says that Rong's two sons did not take leave and knew they would certainly die together; this can still be considered somewhat reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Songzhi believes: The Shiyu says that Rong's two sons did not take leave and knew they would certainly die together; this can still be considered somewhat reasonable.

sentences.zh: 如孙盛之言，诚所未譬。

translations.literal: As for Sun Sheng's account, truly I do not understand it.
translations.idiomatic: As for Sun Sheng's account, truly I do not understand it.

sentences.zh: 八岁小儿，能玄了祸福，聪明特达，卓然既远，则其忧乐之情，宜其有过成人，安有见父收执而曾无变容，弈棋不起，若在暇豫者乎？

translations.literal: If eight-year-old children could profoundly understand disaster and fortune, with intelligence especially penetrating and distinction already far-reaching, then their feelings of grief and joy ought to have surpassed those of adults; how could they see their father arrested and yet never change expression, not rise from playing chess, and seem to be at complete leisure?
translations.idiomatic: If eight-year-old children could profoundly understand disaster and fortune, with intelligence especially penetrating and distinction already far-reaching, then their feelings of grief and joy ought to have surpassed those of adults; how could they see their father arrested and yet never change expression, not rise from playing chess, and seem to be at complete leisure?

sentences.zh: 昔申生就命，言不忘父，不以己身将死而废念父之情也。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Shensheng went to his death, his words did not forget his father; he did not, because his own body was about to die, abandon the feeling of thinking of his father.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Shensheng went to his death, his words did not forget his father; he did not, because his own body was about to die, abandon the feeling of thinking of his father.

sentences.zh: 父安犹尚若兹，而况於颠沛哉？

translations.literal: When his father was safe, he was still like this; how much more in distress and danger?
translations.idiomatic: When his father was safe, he was still like this; how much more in distress and danger?

sentences.zh: 盛以此爲美谈，无乃贼夫人之子与！

translations.literal: For Sheng to take this as a fine tale, is this not to injure those men's sons?
translations.idiomatic: For Sheng to take this as a fine tale, is this not to injure those men's sons?

sentences.zh: 盖由好奇情多，而不知言之伤理。

translations.literal: It was probably because his fondness for the strange was excessive, and he did not know that his words injured principle.
translations.idiomatic: It was probably because his fondness for the strange was excessive, and he did not know that his words injured principle.

sentences.zh: 南阳许攸、

translations.literal: Xu You of Nanyang,
translations.idiomatic: Xu You of Nanyang—

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：攸字子远，少与袁绍及太祖善。

translations.literal: 〈The Brief History of Wei records: You, courtesy name Ziyuan, in youth was on good terms with both Yuan Shao and the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Weilüe states that Xu You, courtesy Ziyuan, was friendly in youth with Yuan Shao and Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 初平中随绍在冀州，尝在坐席言议。

translations.literal: In the Chuping years he followed Shao in Ji Province and once spoke from his seat at deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: During Chuping he attended Yuan Shao in Ji and joined council discussions.

sentences.zh: 官渡之役，谏绍勿与太祖相攻，語在《绍傳》。

translations.literal: At the Guandu campaign he remonstrated with Shao not to attack the Grand Progenitor; the words are in Shao's biography.
translations.idiomatic: At Guandu he urged Yuan Shao not to strike Cao Cao; the detail appears in Yuan Shao's memoir.

sentences.zh: 绍自以强盛，必欲极其兵势。

translations.literal: Shao, deeming himself powerful, was determined to exhaust the possibilities of military force.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao, confident in his strength, meant to push every military advantage.

sentences.zh: 攸知不可爲谋，乃亡诣太祖。

translations.literal: You knew plans could not be made there and fled to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing counsel was useless, Xu You defected to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 绍破走，及后得冀州，攸有功焉。

translations.literal: After Shao was broken and fled, and afterward Ji Province was taken, You had merit therein.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao broke and fled and Ji Province later fell, Xu You earned credit.

sentences.zh: 攸自恃勋劳，时与太祖相戏，每在席，不自限齐，至呼太祖小字，曰：“某甲，卿不得我，不得冀州也。”

translations.literal: You relied on his merit and often bantered with the Grand Progenitor; whenever at banquet he failed to restrain himself and even called the Grand Progenitor by his childhood name, saying, 'Without me you would not have gotten Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He traded on those deeds and japed with Cao Cao; at feasts he forgot restraint and addressed him by childhood name, saying without him Cao Cao would never have taken Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 太祖笑曰：“汝言是也。”

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor laughed and said, 'What you say is right.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed and agreed he spoke truth.

sentences.zh: 然内嫌之。

translations.literal: Yet inwardly he resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet inwardly he bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 其后從行出鄴東門，顧謂左右曰：『此家非得我，則不得出入此門也。』

translations.literal: Later, accompanying him on an outing out the east gate of Ye, he turned to those at his side and said, 'This fellow—without me he could not pass in and out this gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, leaving Ye's east gate together, he told attendants that without him that man would never walk through that gate.

sentences.zh: 人有白者，遂見收之。

translations.literal: Someone informed on him, and he was then seized.〉
translations.idiomatic: An informer repeated it and he was arrested.〉

sentences.zh: 娄圭，皆以恃舊不虔見誅。

translations.literal: Lou Gui—all because they relied on old familiarity without reverence were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Gui—both died because they presumed on old acquaintance and showed disrespect.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：娄圭字子伯，少與太祖有舊。

translations.literal: 〈The Brief History of Wei records: Lou Gui, courtesy name Zibo, in youth had old ties with the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Weilüe states that Lou Gui, courtesy Zibo, had known Cao Cao since youth.

sentences.zh: 初平中在荆州北界合眾，后诣太祖。

translations.literal: During the Chuping era he gathered followers on the northern border of Jing Province, then went to call on the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuping years Lou Gui raised a band along Jing Province's northern frontier, then presented himself to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖以爲大將，不使典兵，常在坐席言議。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor treated him as a grand general but did not put him in charge of troops; he was regularly present at deliberations from his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao named him a senior general yet withheld battlefield command, keeping him instead at council tables for strategy.

sentences.zh: 及河北平定，随在冀州。

translations.literal: When the region north of the Yellow River was pacified, he accompanied him in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hebei plain was subdued, he followed Cao Cao into Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 其后太祖从诸子出游，子伯时亦随从。

translations.literal: Later, when the Grand Progenitor went out touring with his sons, Zibo also accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cao Cao rode out with his sons for pleasure, and Lou Zibo went along.

sentences.zh: 子伯顾谓左右曰：“此家父子，如今日爲乐也。”

translations.literal: Zibo turned to those beside him and said, 'This father and sons—what pleasure they take today.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zibo remarked to attendants how happily that father and those sons were enjoying the day.

sentences.zh: 人有白者，太祖以爲有腹诽意，遂收治之。

translations.literal: Someone informed on him; the Grand Progenitor believed he harbored hidden resentment and therefore seized him for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An informer repeated the remark; Cao Cao read it as veiled disloyalty and had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 《吴書》曰：子伯少有猛志，尝叹息曰：“男兒居世，会当得数万兵千匹骑著后耳！”

translations.literal: The 《Wu shu》 says Lou Zibo burned with martial ambition from youth and once sighed that a real man should someday command myriad soldiers and a thousand horses at his back.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Wu shu》 says Lou Zibo burned with martial ambition from youth and once sighed that a real man should someday command myriad soldiers and a thousand horses at his back.

sentences.zh: 侪辈笑之。

translations.literal: His companions laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: His peers mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 后坐藏亡命，被系当死，得逾狱出，捕者追之急，子伯乃变衣服如助捕者，吏不能觉，遂以得免。

translations.literal: Later he was convicted for harboring fugitives, bound awaiting death; he broke out of prison; pursuers pressed hard; Zibo changed clothes to resemble those helping the hunt; the clerks failed to notice him and so he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He later faced execution for sheltering outlaws, broke jail under pursuit, disguised himself as a manhunter, and slipped away unseen.

sentences.zh: 会天下义兵起，子伯亦合众与刘表相依。

translations.literal: When righteous armies rose across the realm, Zibo also gathered followers and attached himself to Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: As loyalist forces rose empire-wide, he raised troops of his own and threw in with Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 后归曹公，遂爲所用，军國大计常与焉。

translations.literal: Later he submitted to Lord Cao and was employed by him; weighty plans of army and state regularly involved him.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually entered Cao Cao's service and sat in on the gravest civil and military decisions.

sentences.zh: 刘表亡，曹公向荆州。

translations.literal: When Liu Biao died, Lord Cao marched toward Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Biao's death Cao Cao advanced on Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 表子琮降，以节迎曹公，诸将皆疑诈，曹公以问子伯。

translations.literal: Liu Biao's son Cong surrendered and greeted Lord Cao bearing the tally of authority; the generals all suspected a ruse; Lord Cao asked Zibo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong came out with the imperial baton to surrender; the commanders smelled a trap, so Cao Cao sought Lou Zibo's reading.

sentences.zh: 子伯曰：“天下扰攘，各贪王命以自重，今以节来，是必至诚。”

translations.literal: Zibo said, 'The realm is in turmoil; each lord craves royal mandate to bolster himself—now they deliver the tally; this must be utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zibo argued that in chaos every warlord waves the emperor's warrant for legitimacy—bringing the tally proved earnest intent.

sentences.zh: 曹公曰：“大善。”

translations.literal: Lord Cao said, 'Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied, 'Splendid."

sentences.zh: 遂进兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced the army.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed the army forward on that advice.

sentences.zh: 宠秩子伯，家累千金，曰：“娄子伯富乐于孤，但势不如孤耳！”

translations.literal: He showered honors on Zibo until his household piled up a thousand in gold, saying, 'Lou Zibo is as rich and merry as I—only his power cannot match mine!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao heaped rewards on him until the Lou clan held a fortune in gold, joking that Lou Zibo rivaled him in wealth and pleasure if not in authority.

sentences.zh: 从破馬超等，子伯功爲多。

translations.literal: In the campaign that defeated Ma Chao and others, Zibo's merit ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zibo's contributions stood highest in the victory over Ma Chao and company.

sentences.zh: 曹公常叹曰：“子伯之计，孤不及也。”

translations.literal: Lord Cao often sighed, 'In Zibo's stratagems I cannot match him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao often admitted Lou Zibo outthought him.

sentences.zh: 后与南郡习授同载，见曹公出，授曰：“父子如此，何其快耶！”

translations.literal: Later, riding in the same carriage with Xi Shou of Nan Commandery, seeing Lord Cao emerge, Shou said, 'Father and sons like this—how exhilarating!
translations.idiomatic: Later he shared a cart with Xi Shou from Nan commandery; watching Cao Cao appear with his sons, Xi Shou exclaimed at how splendid they looked.

sentences.zh: 子伯曰：“居世间，当自爲之，而但观他人乎！”

translations.literal: Zibo said, 'Living in the world, should one achieve greatness oneself or merely watch others do it!
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zibo answered that a man ought to seize greatness himself rather than gawk at another man's triumph.

sentences.zh: 授乃白之，遂见诛。

translations.literal: Shou thereupon informed on him, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shou reported the remark, and Lou Zibo was put to death.

sentences.zh: 鱼豢曰：古人有言曰：‘得鸟者，罗之一目也，然張一目之罗，终不得鸟矣。

translations.literal: Yu Huan said: An ancient had a saying: "For one who catches a bird, it is one mesh of the net; yet if one spreads a net of one mesh, in the end he will not catch a bird.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan said: An ancient had a saying: "For one who catches a bird, it is one mesh of the net; yet if one spreads a net of one mesh, in the end he will not catch a bird.

sentences.zh: 鸟能远飞，远飞者，六翮之力也，然无众毛之助，则飞不远矣。

translations.literal: A bird cannot be without one mesh, and one mesh cannot get the bird.
translations.idiomatic: A bird cannot be without one mesh, and one mesh cannot get the bird.

sentences.zh: ’以此推之，大魏之作，虽有功臣，亦未必非兹辈胥附之由也。〉

translations.literal: Pushing from this, although the rise of Great Wei had meritorious ministers, it was not necessarily unrelated to the clinging support of men of this sort."〉
translations.idiomatic: Pushing from this, although the rise of Great Wei had meritorious ministers, it was not necessarily unrelated to the clinging support of men of this sort."〉

sentences.zh: 而琰最爲世所痛惜，至今冤之。

translations.literal: Yet Yan was the one the age most lamented; to this day people deem him wronged.
