translations.idiomatic: It was Cui Yan whom contemporaries mourned most; posterity still calls his fate unjust.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：琰兄孙谅，字士文，以简素称，仕晋爲尚書大鸿胪。

translations.literal: 〈《Shiyu》 names Yan's grandnephew Liang, style Shiwen, celebrated for austerity, who rose under Jin to minister of the masters of writing and grand herald.
translations.idiomatic: 〈《Shiyu》 names Yan's grandnephew Liang, style Shiwen, celebrated for austerity, who rose under Jin to minister of the masters of writing and grand herald.

sentences.zh: 荀绰《冀州记》云谅即琰之孙也。〉

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's 《Ji Province gazetteer》 identifies Liang as Yan's grandson.〉
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo's 《Ji Province gazetteer》 identifies Liang as Yan's grandson.〉

sentences.zh: 毛玠字孝先，陳留平丘人也。

translations.literal: Mao Jie, courtesy Xiaoxian, was a man of Pingqiu in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jie, courtesy Xiaoxian, came from Pingqiu in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 少爲县吏，以清公称。

translations.literal: In youth he was a county clerk, famed for purity and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: As a young clerk he earned a reputation for honest impartiality.

sentences.zh: 将避乱荆州，未至，闻刘表政令不明，遂往鲁阳。

translations.literal: He was about to flee turmoil to Jing Province; before he arrived he heard Liu Biao's government was ill ordered; he therefore went to Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bound for Jing Province to escape chaos, he turned aside to Luyang on hearing Liu Biao ruled weakly.

sentences.zh: 太祖临兗州，辟爲治中从事。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor took Yan Province he summoned him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao recruited him as administrative adviser when he entered Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 玠語太祖曰：“今天下分崩，國主迁移，生民废业，饥馑流亡，公家无经岁之储，百姓无安固之志，难以持久。

translations.literal: Mao Jie said to Grand Progenitor, "Now the realm is divided and collapsing, the lord of the state has moved, the living people have abandoned their work, famine has sent them wandering, the public house has no stores for a full year, and the common people have no settled resolve. It will be hard to hold out long.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jie said to Grand Progenitor, "Now the realm is divided and collapsing, the lord of the state has moved, the living people have abandoned their work, famine has sent them wandering, the public house has no stores for a full year, and the common people have no settled resolve. It will be hard to hold out long.

sentences.zh: 今袁绍、刘表，虽士民众强，皆无经远之虑，未有树基建本者也。

translations.literal: Now Yuan Shao and Liu Biao, though their armies and people are strong, both have no long-term plans and have not established a foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yuan Shao and Liu Biao, though their armies and people are strong, both have no long-term plans and have not established a foundation.

sentences.zh: 夫兵义者胜，守位以财，宜奉天子以令不臣，脩耕植，畜军资，如此则霸王之业可成也。”

translations.literal: Righteous armies prevail, and wealth preserves position. You should uphold the Son of Heaven in order to command those who are not subjects, repair plowing and planting, and store military supplies. If you do this, the enterprise of hegemon and king can be completed."
translations.idiomatic: Righteous armies prevail, and wealth preserves position. You should uphold the Son of Heaven in order to command those who are not subjects, repair plowing and planting, and store military supplies. If you do this, the enterprise of hegemon and king can be completed."

sentences.zh: 太祖敬纳其言，转幕府功曹。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor respectfully accepted his counsel and transferred him to merit evaluator on the headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao adopted the advice and moved him onto headquarters staff as merit assessor.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲司空丞相，玠尝爲東曹掾，与崔琰并典选举。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor was minister of works and chancellor, Jie served as aide in the eastern bureau and with Cui Yan jointly supervised appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Cao Cao as minister of works and chancellor, Mao Jie served in the eastern bureau alongside Cui Yan, both directing personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 其所举用，皆清正之士，虽於时有盛名而行不由本者，终莫得进。

translations.literal: Those he recommended were all upright and pure; though some enjoyed great fame at the time yet conduct did not rest on substance, in the end none advanced.
translations.idiomatic: His nominees were consistently honest; flashy reputations without moral root never passed his gate.

sentences.zh: 务以俭率人，由是天下之士莫不以廉节自励，虽贵宠之臣，舆服不敢过度。

translations.literal: He strove to lead others through frugality; hence gentlemen across the realm took incorruptibility as their spur; even favored ministers dared not exceed regulation in carriages and dress.
translations.idiomatic: His personal austerity set the tone until officials empire-wide prized integrity and even favorites kept coaches and robes within statute.

sentences.zh: 太祖叹曰：“用人如此，使天下人自治，吾复何爲哉！”

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sighed, 'Employ men thus—let the realm govern itself—what further need have I!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marveled that if appointments stayed this principled, the world would rule itself without him.

sentences.zh: 文帝爲五官将，亲自诣玠，属所亲眷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was general of the five offices, he personally visited Jie and entrusted him with a favored relative.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir as general of the five offices, Cao Pi went in person to ask Mao Jie to advance a favorite connection.

sentences.zh: 玠答曰：“老臣以能守职，幸得免戾，今所说人非迁次，是以不敢奉命。”

translations.literal: Jie replied, 'This old minister by keeping duty has luckily escaped blame; the man you speak of is not due for promotion—I dare not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jie refused: an aged official who survived by scruples could not promote someone out of turn.

sentences.zh: 大军还鄴，议所并省。

translations.literal: When the great army returned to Ye, they debated which offices to merge and abolish.
translations.idiomatic: After the host returned to Ye, ministers debated which bureaus to consolidate.

sentences.zh: 玠请谒不行，时人惮之，咸欲省東曹。

translations.literal: Jie declined audiences; people feared him; all wished to abolish the eastern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mao Jie would grant no private hearings, rivals feared him and pushed to dissolve the eastern bureau.

sentences.zh: 乃共白曰：“旧西曹爲上，東曹爲次，宜省東曹。”

translations.literal: They jointly reported: 'Formerly the western bureau ranked first, the eastern second—we ought to abolish the eastern.
translations.idiomatic: They argued canon placed the western bureau above the eastern and urged cutting the latter.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其情，令曰：“日出於東，月盛於東，凡人言方，亦复先東，何以省東曹？”

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor knew their motive and ordered: 'The sun rises in the east, the moon waxes in the east; when common men speak of directions they begin with east—why abolish the eastern bureau?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao saw through the ploy and countered that cosmology and speech alike honored the east—hardly grounds to erase its office.

sentences.zh: 遂省西曹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abolished the western bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the western bureau instead.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖平柳城，班所获器物，特以素屏风素冯几赐玠，曰：“君有古人之风，故赐君古人之服。”

translations.literal: When first the Grand Progenitor pacified Liucheng, distributing captured goods, he specially gave Jie plain screens and a plain armrest-stool, saying, 'You have the manner of antiquity—therefore I grant you the furnishings of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: After Liucheng fell, Cao Cao singled out Mao Jie for undyed screens and a simple armrest, praising his antique austerity with fitting gifts.

sentences.zh: 玠居显位，常布衣蔬食，抚育孤兄子甚笃，赏赐以振施贫族，家无所馀。

translations.literal: Jie held eminent rank yet wore cloth and ate coarse food; he nurtured his elder brother's orphaned son with deep care; he used rewards to relieve poor kin; nothing remained in his household.
translations.idiomatic: Though powerful, he dressed as a commoner, ate plainly, raised his widowed brother's son devotedly, and funneled stipends to needy kin until nothing stayed at home.

sentences.zh: 迁右军师。

translations.literal: He was promoted right army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right army adviser.

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，爲尚書仆射，复典选举。

translations.literal: When Wei was first founded he became vice director of the masters of writing and again supervised appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Wei established him as vice director of the masters of writing with renewed charge over promotions.

sentences.zh: 〈先贤行状曰：玠雅亮公正，在官清恪。

translations.literal: 〈《Conduct of earlier worthies》 calls him magnanimous, candid, and scrupulous in every post.
translations.idiomatic: 〈《Conduct of earlier worthies》 calls him magnanimous, candid, and scrupulous in every post.

sentences.zh: 其典选举，拔贞实，斥華伪，进逊行，抑阿党。

translations.literal: In supervising appointments he elevated the genuine, rejected flashy fraud, advanced retiring conduct, and checked faction.
translations.idiomatic: Over selections he favored substance over show, humility over swagger, and struck at cliques.

sentences.zh: 诸宰官治民功绩不著而私财丰足者，皆免黜停废，久不选用。

translations.literal: Magistrates whose governance showed no merit yet private wealth abounded were all dismissed and shelved, long unchosen thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: County heads who enriched themselves without benefiting the people lost rank for years.

sentences.zh: 于时四海翕然，莫不励行。

translations.literal: Then all within the seas aligned; none failed to brace their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The empire snapped to attention; everyone tightened discipline.

sentences.zh: 至乃长吏还者，垢面羸衣，常乘柴车。

translations.literal: Even returning senior officials went unkempt in threadbare clothes, often riding firewood carts.
translations.idiomatic: District chiefs coming off assignment arrived unwashed in rags, often aboard hay carts.

sentences.zh: 军吏入府，朝服徒行。

translations.literal: Army clerks entering offices wore court dress yet walked on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Military clerks entered yamen in court robes but on foot.

sentences.zh: 人拟壶飧之絜，家象濯缨之操，贵者无秽欲之累，贱者绝奸货之求，吏絜于上，俗移乎下，民到于今称之。〉

translations.literal: People matched the purity of offering a meal in a pitcher; households mirrored the integrity of washing the cap-tassel—the eminent shed coarse desire; the humble renounced grasping gain; officials were pure above and custom shifted below; the people praise it to this day.〉
translations.idiomatic: Citizens aspired to the spotless courtesy of a roadside meal; families cultivated the 《Songs》 ideal of clean motives—nobles shed greed, commoners shunned graft; purity flowed down from the clerks and manners followed; posterity still applauds it.〉

sentences.zh: 时太子未定，而临菑侯植有宠，玠密谏曰：“近者袁绍以嫡庶不分，覆宗灭國。

translations.literal: At the time, the heir apparent had not yet been settled, and the Marquis of Linzi, Cao Zhi, was favored. Mao Jie secretly remonstrated, saying, "Recently Yuan Shao, because he did not distinguish legitimate heir and collateral sons, overturned his clan and destroyed his state.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, the heir apparent had not yet been settled, and the Marquis of Linzi, Cao Zhi, was favored. Mao Jie secretly remonstrated, saying, "Recently Yuan Shao, because he did not distinguish legitimate heir and collateral sons, overturned his clan and destroyed his state.

sentences.zh: 废立大事，非所宜闻。”

translations.literal: Deposing and establishing heirs is a great matter, and not something that should be heard of."
translations.idiomatic: Deposing and establishing heirs is a great matter, and not something that should be heard of."

sentences.zh: 后群僚会，玠起更衣，太祖目指曰：“此古所谓國之司直，我之周昌也。”

translations.literal: Later at a gathering of officials Jie rose to change garments; the Grand Progenitor signaled with his eyes and said, 'This is what antiquity calls the state's straight judge—my Zhou Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Mao Jie left a council to change clothes, Cao Cao pointed him out as the court's blunt conscience—his own Zhou Chang.

sentences.zh: 崔琰既死，玠内不悦。

translations.literal: When Cui Yan died, Jie was inwardly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jie nursed resentment after Cui Yan's death.

sentences.zh: 后有白玠者：“出见黥面反者，其妻子没爲官奴婢，玠言曰‘使天不雨者盖此也’。”

translations.literal: Later someone accused Jie: 'Going out he saw tattoo-faced rebels whose wives and children had been seized as government slaves; Jie said, 'Those who make Heaven withhold rain are surely such as these.'
translations.idiomatic: An accuser claimed Mao Jie blamed drought on tattoo-faced traitors whose families served as penal slaves.

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒，收玠付狱。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was furious, seized Jie, and handed him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Cao Cao jailed him.

sentences.zh: 大理锺繇诘玠曰：

translations.literal: Minister of justice Zhong Yao questioned Jie:
translations.idiomatic: Court inspector Zhong Yao interrogated him:

sentences.zh: 自古圣帝明王，罪及妻子。

translations.literal: From antiquity sacred emperors and enlightened kings extended punishment to wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Since high antiquity sage kings punished kin along with the culprit.

sentences.zh: 書云：‘左不共左，右不共右，予则孥戮女。

translations.literal: The Documents says, "If the left does not attend to the left, or the right does not attend to the right, I will execute you with your wives and children."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "If the left does not attend to the left, or the right does not attend to the right, I will execute you with your wives and children."

sentences.zh: ’司寇之职，男子入于罪隶，女子入于舂□。

translations.literal: The office of minister of crime assigns men to criminal servitude and women to pounding grain.
translations.idiomatic: The office of minister of crime assigns men to criminal servitude and women to pounding grain.

sentences.zh: 汉律，罪人妻子没爲奴婢，黥面。

translations.literal: Han statutes: a culprit's wife and children were confiscated as slaves and bondmaids with tattooed faces.
translations.idiomatic: Han law likewise branded traitors' families and bound them as government slaves.

sentences.zh: 汉法所行黥墨之刑，存於古典。

translations.literal: The tattooing ink punishment Han applied survives in classical antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Facial branding rested on precedent honored since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今真奴婢祖先有罪，虽历百世，犹有黥面供官，一以宽良民之命，二以宥并罪之辜。

translations.literal: Now true slaves and maids whose ancestors sinned—even after a hundred generations—still bear tattooed faces while serving office: first to spare good subjects, second to forgive collective guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping branded bondsmen honors both mercy toward the innocent and acknowledgment of inherited guilt.

sentences.zh: 此何以负於神明之意，而当致旱？

translations.literal: How does this betray the intent of gods and spirits such that it should bring drought?
translations.idiomatic: How could such policy insult Heaven enough to stop the rains?

sentences.zh: 案典谋，急恆寒若，舒恆燠若，宽则亢阳，所以爲旱。

translations.literal: According to the canon on counsels, severity brings constant cold-like chill, laxity brings constant heat-like warmth; indulgence brings blazing yang—that is how drought arises.
translations.idiomatic: The counsels link harsh rule with chill and lax rule with drought—blazing yang follows loosened discipline.

sentences.zh: 玠之吐言，以爲宽邪，以爲急也？

translations.literal: Were Jie's words meant as lax indulgence or as severity?
translations.idiomatic: Did Mao Jie intend laxity or severity?

sentences.zh: 急当阴霖，何以反旱？

translations.literal: If severity, steady gloomy rain should follow—why instead drought?
translations.idiomatic: If severity, skies should weep—why this sun-scorch instead?

sentences.zh: 成汤圣世，野无生草，周宣令主，旱魃爲虐。

translations.literal: In Cheng Tang's sage age the wilds bore no grass; King Xuan of Zhou was a fine lord yet the drought demon ravaged.
translations.idiomatic: Even Cheng Tang's reign knew barren fields; King Xuan faced the scourge of drought-fiends.

sentences.zh: 亢旱以来，积三十年，归咎黥面，爲相值不？

translations.literal: For this stubborn drought, thirty years have piled up—blaming tattooed faces, does that explanation fit?
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years of drought cannot hinge on branded servants alone.

sentences.zh: 卫人伐邢，师兴而雨，罪恶无徵，何以应天？

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Xing, rain fell as the army rose—no proof of crime—how does one answer Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Wei invaded Xing and rain followed without proven guilt—what cosmic verdict is that?

sentences.zh: 玠讥谤之言，流於下民，不悦之声，上闻圣听。

translations.literal: Jie's mocking words circulated among the common people; sounds of displeasure reached the sage listener.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jie's barbs reached the streets and echoed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 玠之吐言，势不独語，时见黥面，凡爲几人？

translations.literal: Jie's words could not have been spoken alone—when he saw tattooed faces, how many were there in all?
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao demanded how many branded faces Mao Jie could have seen if he spoke aloud.

sentences.zh: 黥面奴婢，所识知邪？

translations.literal: The tattooed slaves and maids—did he know them?
translations.idiomatic: Did he recognize those bondsmen?

sentences.zh: 何缘得见，对之叹言？

translations.literal: By what chance did he see them and sigh speech toward them?
translations.idiomatic: How did he encounter them to sigh in their presence?

sentences.zh: 时以語谁？

translations.literal: To whom did he speak?
translations.idiomatic: Who overheard him?

sentences.zh: 见答云何？

translations.literal: What reply did he receive?
translations.idiomatic: What answer came back?

sentences.zh: 以何日月？

translations.literal: On what day and month?
translations.idiomatic: Which day?

sentences.zh: 於何处所？

translations.literal: At what place?
translations.idiomatic: Where?

sentences.zh: 事已发露，不得隐欺，具以状对。

translations.literal: The matter is exposed; you may not conceal or deceive—answer fully with the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Expose everything now—no evasions.

sentences.zh: 玠曰：

translations.literal: Jie said:
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jie replied:

sentences.zh: 臣闻萧生缢死，困於石显；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard Xiao Wangzhi strangled himself, trapped by Shi Xian;
translations.idiomatic: He cited Xiao Wangzhi driven to hang by Shi Xian;

sentences.zh: 贾子放外，谗在绛、灌；

translations.literal: Jia Yi was cast to the frontier, slander coming from Zhou Bo and Guan Ying;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi banished on Zhou Bo and Guan Ying's malice;

sentences.zh: 白起赐劍於杜邮；

translations.literal: Bai Qi received the sword at Duyou;
translations.idiomatic: Bai Qi forced to die at Duyou;

sentences.zh: 晁错致诛於東市；

translations.literal: Chao Cuo met execution at the eastern market;
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo cut down at the eastern market;

sentences.zh: 伍员绝命於吴都：斯数子者，或妒其前，或害其后。

translations.literal: Wu Zixu met death in the Wu capital: these several men were envied ahead or harmed from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu executed at Wu—each victim undone by jealousy fore or aft.

sentences.zh: 臣垂龆执简，累勤取官，职在机近，人事所窜。

translations.literal: Your servant from childhood held the brush, by diligent steps gained office; duty lies near the pivot—human affairs breed displacement.
translations.idiomatic: He himself had risen since boyhood through diligence beside the throne, where intrigue never sleeps.

sentences.zh: 属臣以私，无势不绝，語臣以冤，无细不理。

translations.literal: Attach private motives to your servant—without power nothing stops it; speak of grievance—no trifle goes unhandled.
translations.idiomatic: Private spite stalked him endlessly; every whisper of injustice reached his desk.

sentences.zh: 人情淫利，爲法所禁，法禁于利，势能害之。

translations.literal: Human hearts lust for profit—law forbids it; where law forbids profit, power can harm this.
translations.idiomatic: Law blocks greed, yet influence still twists justice.

sentences.zh: 青蝇横生，爲臣作谤，谤臣之人，势不在他。

translations.literal: Blue flies swarm abroad—they fabricate slander against your servant; those who slander—power lies nowhere else.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderous flies buzzed because rivals wielded leverage, not truth.

sentences.zh: 昔王叔、陳生争正王廷，宣子平理。

translations.literal: Once Wang Shu and Chen Sheng disputed rectitude in the royal court; Xuanzi settled it.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled how Zhao Dun judged Wang Shu and Chen Sheng's feud.

sentences.zh: 命举其契，是非有宜，曲直有所，春秋嘉焉，是以書之。

translations.literal: The 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 celebrated how justice sorted crooked from straight once the covenant tablet surfaced.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 celebrated how justice sorted crooked from straight once the covenant tablet surfaced.

sentences.zh: 臣不言此，无有时、人。

translations.literal: Your servant does not speak thus without occasion or witness.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted he had neither invented the tale nor lacked corroboration.

sentences.zh: 说臣此言，必有徵要。

translations.literal: Whoever repeats your servant's words must have proof.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone repeating his defense must produce evidence.

sentences.zh: 乞蒙宣子之辨，而求王叔之对。

translations.literal: I beg to receive Xuanzi's discrimination and seek Wang Shu's counterargument.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for the sort of hearing Zhao Dun gave Wang Shu against Chen Sheng.

sentences.zh: 若臣以曲闻，即刑之日，方之安驷之赠；

translations.literal: If your servant is heard as crooked, then on the day of execution compare it to the gift of the peace-team horses;
translations.idiomatic: If he stood convicted of distortion, let execution parallel the tribute of gentle carriage horses.

sentences.zh: 赐劍之来，比之重赏之惠。

translations.literal: when the sword arrives, compare it to the grace of a weighty reward.
translations.idiomatic: When the blade came, treat it as the bounty owed a vindicated minister.

sentences.zh: 谨以状对。

translations.literal: Respectfully I answer with this deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Here ends his sworn reply.

sentences.zh: 时桓阶、和洽进言救玠。

translations.literal: At the time Huan Jie and He Qia advanced arguments to save Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Jie and He Qia intervened on Mao Jie's behalf.

sentences.zh: 玠遂免黜，卒于家。

translations.literal: Jie thereupon escaped dismissal and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jie was spared removal and died in retirement.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：魏武於是失政刑矣。

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng says: thereby Wei Wu lost proper governance and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sun Sheng remarks that Cao Cao forfeited sound justice at that moment.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱『明折庶獄』，《傳》有『舉直措枉』，庶獄明則國無怨民，枉直當則民無不服，未有徵青蝇之浮聲，信浸润之谮诉，可以允釐四海，惟清缉熙者也。

translations.literal: The Changes praises 'clearly deciding the myriad lawsuits'; the Traditions records 'raising the straight and setting aside the crooked'—when lawsuits are clear the state harbors no resentful people; when crooked and straight are fit none refuse submission—never yet did accepting the buzzing of blue flies or trusting soaking slander win orderly rule within the four seas and pure radiance alone.
translations.idiomatic: Classics demand lucid trials and promotion of the upright; unjust verdicts breed popular wrath—yet Cao Cao trusted malicious rumor instead of clearing courts across the realm.

sentences.zh: 昔者漢高獄萧何，出復相之，玠之一责，永見摈放，二主度量，豈不殊哉！

translations.literal: Formerly Han Gaozu imprisoned Xiao He yet released him to be chancellor again; one reproach of Jie brought perpetual banishment—how the two lords' magnanimity did not match!〉
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bang jailed Xiao He yet restored him; one Mao Jie indictment meant exile forever—what a gulf between those rulers!〉

sentences.zh: 太祖賜棺器钱帛，拜子机郎中。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor granted coffin furnishings, cash, and silk, and appointed his son Ji gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent burial goods and appointed Mao Ji as court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 徐奕字季才，東莞人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yi, courtesy Jicai, was a man of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi, courtesy Jicai, hailed from Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 避难江東，孙策礼命之。

translations.literal: He fled turmoil to east of the Yangzi; Sun Ce treated him with ritual summons.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking refuge east of the river, he received Sun Ce's courteous summons.

sentences.zh: 奕改姓名，微服还本郡。

translations.literal: Yi changed his name and in plain clothes returned to his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed an alias, traveled incognito, and slipped back to his native district.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲司空，辟爲掾属，从西征馬超。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor was minister of works he summoned him as staff aide and took him west against Ma Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao as minister of works enlisted him for staff duty on the western campaign against Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 超破，军还。

translations.literal: When Chao was broken the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Chao's defeat the host marched home.

sentences.zh: 时关中新服，未甚安，留奕爲丞相长史，镇抚西京，西京称其威信。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong had newly submitted and was not yet settled; Yi was retained as chief clerk of the chancellor to pacify and reassure the western capital; the western capital praised his awe-inspiring trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Newly pacified Guanzhong still trembled; Xu Yi stayed as chief clerk to steady the western metropolis, where men hailed his commanding integrity.

sentences.zh: 转爲雍州刺史，复还爲東曹属。

translations.literal: He was shifted to governor of Yong Province, then returned as aide in the eastern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rotated to Yong governor, then back to the eastern bureau staff.

sentences.zh: 丁仪等见宠於时，并害之，而奕终不爲动。

translations.literal: Ding Yi and others were favored at court and together harmed him, yet Yi to the end was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Court favorites Ding Yi schemed against him, but Xu Yi never bent.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書曰：或谓奕曰：“夫以史鱼之直，孰与蘧伯玉之智？

translations.literal: 〈Wei shu records: Someone said to Yi, 'Between Shi Yu's bluntness and Qu Boyu's wisdom—which excels?
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shu relates a question whether Shi Yu's blunt integrity surpassed Qu Boyu's tact.

sentences.zh: 丁仪方贵重，宜思所以下之。”

translations.literal: Ding Yi is rising to power—you ought to consider how to humble yourself before him.
translations.idiomatic: With Ding Yi ascendant, Yi was urged to curry favor below him.

sentences.zh: 奕曰：“以公明圣，仪岂得行其伪乎！

translations.literal: Yi said, 'Given the lord's enlightened sagacity, how could Yi practice deception!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi answered that under a sage ruler Ding Yi could not rule by falsity.

sentences.zh: 且奸以事君者，吾所能御也，子宁以他规我。”

translations.literal: Moreover crafty ministers serving the lord—those I know how to resist; you had better advise me on something else.
translations.idiomatic: Sycophants were foes he could handle; better counsel another topic.

sentences.zh: 《傅子》曰：武皇帝，至明也。

translations.literal: The Fu zi states: Martial Emperor was supremely perspicacious.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan's Fu zi adds that Cao Cao was extraordinarily clear-sighted.

sentences.zh: 崔琰、徐奕，一時清賢，皆以忠信顯於魏朝；

translations.literal: Cui Yan and Xu Yi, pure worthies of their day, both shone in Wei through loyalty and trustworthiness;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan and Xu Yi epitomized loyal candor at court.

sentences.zh: 丁儀間之，徐奕失位而崔琰被誅。

translations.literal: Ding Yi came between them—Xu Yi lost office while Cui Yan suffered execution.〉
translations.idiomatic: Ding Yi's intrigues cost Xu Yi his post and Cui Yan his life.〉

sentences.zh: 出爲魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖征孙权，徙爲留府长史，谓奕曰：“君之忠亮，古人不过也，然微太严。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Sun Quan he transferred him to chief clerk of the rear headquarters and told Yi, 'Your loyalty and brightness surpass the ancients—yet you are slightly too severe.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilizing against Sun Quan, Cao Cao named Xu Yi rear headquarters chief clerk, praising his loyalty yet chiding his harshness.

sentences.zh: 昔西门豹佩韦以自缓，夫能以柔弱制刚强者，望之於君也。

translations.literal: Long ago Ximen Bao wore soft leather to moderate himself—one who can govern hardness with softness is what is hoped from you.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Ximen Bao softening his temper with a leather sash—flexibility curbing rigidity was what he asked.

sentences.zh: 今使君统留事，孤无复还顾之忧也。”

translations.literal: Now that you oversee rear headquarters affairs, this solitary one has no further worry about returning.
translations.idiomatic: With Xu Yi guarding Ye, Cao Cao claimed freedom from rear-area fears.

sentences.zh: 魏國既建，爲尚書，复典选举，迁尚書令。

translations.literal: When Wei had been founded he became minister of the masters of writing, again supervised appointments, and advanced to director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he rose through minister of personnel to director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 太祖征汉中，魏讽等谋反，中尉杨俊左迁。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned in Hanzhong, Wei Feng and others plotted rebellion; commandant of the capital Yang Jun was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hanzhong expedition Wei Feng's plot demoted capital commandant Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 太祖叹曰：“讽所以敢生乱心，以吾爪牙之臣无遏奸防谋者故也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sighed, 'Feng dared cherish rebellion because among my talon-and-fang ministers none blocked treachery or forestalled plots.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao blamed the coup on guards who failed to sniff out intrigue.

sentences.zh: 安得如诸葛丰者，使代俊乎！”

translations.literal: How can I obtain someone like Zhuge Feng to replace Jun!
translations.idiomatic: He wished for another Zhuge Feng to fill the post.

sentences.zh: 桓阶曰：“徐奕其人也。”

translations.literal: Huan Jie said, 'Xu Yi is the man.'
translations.idiomatic: Huan Jie nominated Xu Yi.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃以奕爲中尉，手令曰：“昔楚有子玉，文公爲之侧席而坐；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor therefore made Yi commandant of the capital, issuing a handwritten order: 'Ancient Chu had Ziyu—Duke Wen sat sideways for fear of him;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao appointed him capital commandant, likening him to Chu commander Ziyu who made Duke Wen edge his seat.

sentences.zh: 汲黯在朝，淮南爲之折谋。

translations.literal: Ji An held court—Huainan therefore broke its plots.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An's presence in court foiled Huainan's schemes.

sentences.zh: 詩称‘邦之司直’，君之谓与！”

translations.literal: The Songs calls "the state's straight judge"—does it mean you!
translations.idiomatic: The Songs line on the state's blunt mirror fit Xu Yi.

sentences.zh: 在职数月，疾笃乞退，拜谏议大夫，卒。

translations.literal: After several months in office his illness grew grave and he begged retirement; he was appointed grandee remonstrant and died.
translations.idiomatic: Within months grave illness forced retirement as grandee remonstrant; he soon died.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：文帝每与朝臣会同，未尝不嗟叹，思奕之爲人。

translations.literal: 〈Wei shu records: Emperor Wen whenever meeting courtiers never failed to sigh and ponder Yi's character.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Wei shu notes Cao Pi always mourned Xu Yi's example at council.

sentences.zh: 奕無子，詔以其族子統爲郎，以奉奕後。

translations.literal: Yi had no sons; an edict made his clansman Tong a gentleman of the palace to continue Yi's line.〉
translations.idiomatic: Childless, Xu Yi passed succession to clansman Xu Tong by imperial order.〉

sentences.zh: 何夔字叔龙，陳郡阳夏人也。

translations.literal: He Kui, courtesy Shulong, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He Kui, courtesy Shulong, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖父熙，汉安帝时官至车骑将军。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xi under Han Emperor An rose to chariot-and-cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather He Xi reached chariot-and-cavalry general under Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 〈華峤汉書曰：熙字孟孙，少有大志，不拘小节。

translations.literal: 〈Huaxian's Han shu records: Xi, courtesy Mengsun, in youth had great ambition and did not fuss over small points.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Huaxian's Han shu describes Xi as ambitious and broad-minded from youth.

sentences.zh: 身长八尺五寸，体貌魁梧，善爲容仪。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi five cun tall, massive of frame, skilled at dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Eight chi five in height with a commanding physique and faultless deportment.

sentences.zh: 举孝廉，爲谒者，赞拜殿中，音动左右。

translations.literal: Recommended filial and incorrupt, he served as usher; announcing salutations in the palace hall his voice stirred those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: As filial-incorrupt nominee he became palace usher whose resonant announcements shook the hall.

sentences.zh: 和帝

translations.literal: Emperor He
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He of Han

translations.literal: (editorial gloss reading jia 'fine,' probably standing for jia 'praised')
translations.idiomatic: (a manuscript note reads jia 'fine,' likely corrupt for jia 'praised')

sentences.zh: 之，历位司隶校尉、大司农。

translations.literal: praised him; he progressed through metropolitan commandant and minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: commended him; he rose through metropolitan commandant to minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，南单于与乌丸俱反，以熙行车骑将军征之，累有功。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu the southern Shanyu with the Wuhuan jointly rebelled; Xi was sent acting chariot-and-cavalry general against them and accumulated merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 3 saw the southern Shanyu and Wuhuan revolt; Xi led them as acting chariot-and-cavalry general with repeated success.

sentences.zh: 乌丸请降，单于复称臣如旧。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan sought surrender; the Shanyu again styled himself subject as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan capitulated and the Shanyu renewed vassalage.

sentences.zh: 会熙暴疾卒。〉

translations.literal: Then Xi died suddenly of illness.〉
translations.idiomatic: Xi died abruptly of sickness.〉

sentences.zh: 夔幼丧父，与母兄居，以孝友称。

translations.literal: Kui in childhood lost his father; dwelling with mother and elder brother he was famed for filial piety and brotherly friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, He Kui lived with mother and brother, famed for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 长八尺三寸，容貌矜严。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi three cun tall; his bearing was stern and dignified.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi three with austere, imposing looks.

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：汉末阉宦用事，夔从父衡爲尚書，有直言，由是在党中，诸父兄皆禁锢。

translations.literal: 〈Wei shu records: Late Han eunuchs held power; Kui's uncle by marriage Heng was minister of the masters of writing with blunt speech and therefore fell among the proscribed faction; uncles and elder brothers were all barred from office.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Wei shu adds that when eunuchs purged the court, He's uncle-in-law Heng landed on the blacklist and kin could not serve.

sentences.zh: 夔叹曰：“天地闭，贤人隐。”

translations.literal: Kui sighed, 'Heaven and earth are shut—the worthy hide.
translations.idiomatic: He Kui mourned that heaven sealed its gates and sages withdrew.

sentences.zh: 故不应宰司之命。〉

translations.literal: Therefore he did not answer summons from the ministers.〉
translations.idiomatic: Hence he ignored ministerial appointments.〉

sentences.zh: 避亂淮南。

translations.literal: He fled turmoil to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He escaped chaos into Huainan.

sentences.zh: 后袁术至壽春，辟之，夔不应，然遂爲术所留。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Shu arrived at Shouchun and summoned him; Kui did not respond, yet Shu detained him anyway.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu reaching Shouchun pressed him to serve; though He Kui refused, Shu kept him captive.

sentences.zh: 久之，术與桥蕤俱攻围蕲陽，蕲陽爲太祖固守。

translations.literal: After a long while Shu together with Qiao Rui besieged Qiyang; Qiyang was stubbornly defended for the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Yuan Shu and Qiao Rui invested Qiyang, which held firm for Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 术以夔彼郡人，欲胁令说蕲陽。

translations.literal: Because Kui was a man of that commandery Shu wished to coerce him into persuading Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shu meant to exploit He's local ties to talk the city down.

sentences.zh: 夔謂术謀臣李業曰：『昔柳下惠聞伐國之謀而有忧色，曰「吾聞伐國不問仁人，斯言何爲至於我哉」！』

translations.literal: Kui told Shu's strategist Li Ye, 'Long ago Liuxiahui hearing of a plot to attack another state showed anxious color and said, "I have heard that attacking another state is not discussed with humane men—why should those words reach me!"'
translations.idiomatic: He told Li Ye how Liuxiahui recoiled from invasion plots—humane men never debated such crimes.

sentences.zh: 遂遁匿灊山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fled into hiding on Mount Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He vanished into the Qian Mountains.

sentences.zh: 术知夔终不爲己用，乃止。

translations.literal: Shu knew Kui would never serve himself and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu saw He Kui would never obey and dropped the demand.

sentences.zh: 术从兄山阳太守遗母，夔从姑也，是以虽恨夔而不加害。

translations.literal: Shu's cousin by elder brother, governor of Shanyang, had left behind his mother—she was Kui's aunt by marriage—therefore though Shu resented Kui he did not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Family ties through Shan's prefect—He's aunt—shielded him despite Shu's hatred.

sentences.zh: 建安二年，夔将还鄉里，度术必急追，乃间行得免，明年到本郡。

translations.literal: In the second Jian'an year Kui prepared to return home; judging Shu would surely pursue hotly he traveled by secret routes and escaped; the next year he reached his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an 2 he slipped homeward by back roads before Yuan Shu's pursuit caught him; next year he arrived safe.

sentences.zh: 顷之，太祖辟爲司空掾属。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Grand Progenitor summoned him as staff aide to the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao soon recruited him for ministerial staff.

sentences.zh: 時有傳袁术軍亂者，太祖問夔曰；

translations.literal: At the time someone spread word that Yuan Shu's army was in turmoil; the Grand Progenitor asked Kui:
translations.idiomatic: When rumor claimed Yuan Shu's camp collapsed, Cao Cao queried He Kui:

sentences.zh: “君以爲信不？”

translations.literal: Do you deem it credible?
translations.idiomatic: Do you credit it?

sentences.zh: 夔对曰：“天之所助者顺，人之所助者信。

translations.literal: Kui replied, 'What Heaven aids follows order; what men aid follows trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: He Kui answered that heaven backs the orderly and men back the trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 术无信顺之实，而望天人之助，此不可以得志於天下。

translations.literal: Shu lacks substance of trustworthiness or compliance yet hopes for aid from Heaven and men—by this he cannot realize ambition under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu commanded neither virtue nor legitimacy yet expected cosmic favor—such ambition must fail.

sentences.zh: 夫失道之主，亲戚叛之，而况於左右乎！

translations.literal: When a lord loses the Way even kin rebel—how much more those at his side!
translations.idiomatic: A wicked ruler loses kin first, let alone companions.

sentences.zh: 以夔观之，其乱必矣。”

translations.literal: Judging by what Kui sees, turmoil is certain.
translations.idiomatic: He Kui predicted collapse.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said:
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied:

sentences.zh: 『爲國失賢則亡。

translations.literal: When a state loses worthies it perishes.
translations.idiomatic: States without talent die.

sentences.zh: 君不爲术所用；

translations.literal: You were not employed by Shu;
translations.idiomatic: You refused Yuan Shu;

sentences.zh: 亂，不亦宜乎！”

translations.literal: turmoil—is it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: so his disorder was only natural!

sentences.zh: 太祖性严，掾属公事，往往加杖；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor's nature was strict; staff aides on official business often received beating with sticks;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao beat clerks freely for bureaucratic slips.

sentences.zh: 夔常畜毒药，誓死无辱，是以终不见及。

translations.literal: Kui constantly kept poison handy, swearing death before dishonor—therefore he never suffered it.
translations.idiomatic: He Kui carried poison vowing suicide before flogging—so blows never touched him.

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛曰：夫君使臣以礼，臣事君以忠，是以上下休嘉，道光化洽。

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng says: When the lord employs ministers with ritual and ministers serve with loyalty, high and low share blessing and transforming radiance spreads.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sun Sheng opens by noting ritual loyalty breeds harmony between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 公府掾属，古之造士也，必擢时隽，搜扬英逸，得其人则論道之任隆，非其才则覆餗之患至。

translations.literal: Staff of the duke's offices were antiquity's cultivated gentlemen—one must elevate timely paragons and gather splendid talent; obtaining the right men magnifies counsel's duty, lacking talent brings the peril of overturned stew.
translations.idiomatic: Ducal aides should be elite talent—right picks strengthen policy, wrong picks spill the cauldron.

sentences.zh: 苟有疵衅，刑黜可也。

translations.literal: Should faults appear, punishment or dismissal suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Faults warrant dismissal or stripes.

sentences.zh: 加其捶扑之罚，肃以小惩之戒，岂“导之以德，齐之以礼”之谓与！

translations.literal: To add flogging penalties as petty warning—is this what is meant by 'lead them with virtue, align them with ritual'!
translations.idiomatic: Adding rod discipline hardly matches Confucius's counsel to guide by virtue and ritual.

sentences.zh: 然士之出处，宜度德投趾；

translations.literal: Yet gentlemen choosing office ought to measure virtue before planting foot;
translations.idiomatic: Still, entrants must weigh a lord's virtue before serving.

sentences.zh: 可不之节，必审於所蹈。

translations.literal: when unsure of fit one must examine closely the path trodden.
translations.idiomatic: Uncertain candidates should scrutinize every step.

sentences.zh: 故高尚之徒，抗心於青云之表，岂王侯之所能臣，名器之所羁绁哉！

translations.literal: Hence the lofty lift hearts beyond the clouds—how could mere kings or ceremonial vessels tether them!
translations.idiomatic: The truly high-minded soar beyond royal harness or bronze insignia.

sentences.zh: 自非此族，委身世涂，否泰荣辱，制之由时，故箕子安於孥戮，柳下夷於三黜，萧何、周勃亦在縲绁，夫岂不辱，君命故也。

translations.literal: Unless of that sort, committing body to the world's road, fortune and shame hinge on the hour—thus Jizi accepted penal kin, Liuxiahui endured three dismissals, Xiao He and Zhou Bo even wore fetters—was it not shameful? Yet lordly command compelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Others brave office knowing shame may come—Jizi bore kin punishment, Liuxiahui suffered triple exile, Xiao He and Zhou Bo wore chains—all bowed to sovereign duty.

sentences.zh: 夔知时制，而甘其宠，挟药要君，以避微耻。

translations.literal: Kui grasped the hour's constraints yet sweetly accepted favor, clutching poison to threaten the lord and dodge slight shame.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng faults He Kui for accepting rank yet brandishing poison to blackmail his ruler against minor humiliation.

sentences.zh: 詩云“唯此褊心”，何夔其有焉。

translations.literal: The Songs says 'only this narrow heart'—does it fit He Kui!
translations.idiomatic: The Songs line on petty hearts suits him.

sentences.zh: 放之，可也；

translations.literal: Dismiss him—acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: Banishment would be fair.

sentences.zh: 宥之，非也。〉

translations.literal: pardoning him—is wrong.〉
translations.idiomatic: Absolving him was mistaken.〉

sentences.zh: 出爲城父令。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Chengfu.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Chengfu county.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：自劉備叛后，東南多變。

translations.literal: 〈Wei shu records: After Liu Bei's rebellion the southeast shifted repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Wei shu notes turmoil rippled through the southeast after Liu Bei's revolt.

sentences.zh: 太祖以陳羣爲酂令，夔爲城父令，諸縣皆用名士以镇撫之，其后吏民稍定。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor made Chen Qun magistrate of Zan and Kui magistrate of Chengfu; every county employed famed gentlemen to pacify them; afterward clerks and commoners gradually stabilized.〉
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao posted Chen Qun at Zan and He Kui at Chengfu, staffing counties with reputable scholars until order returned.〉

sentences.zh: 遷長广太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted governor of Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Changguang commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡滨山海，黄巾未平，豪杰多背叛，袁谭就加以官位。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered sea and hills; Yellow Turbans were not yet pacified; stalwarts mostly rebelled; Yuan Tan imposed offices upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal Changguang still swarmed with Turbans and defectors whom Yuan Tan tried to co-opt.

sentences.zh: 长广县人管承，徒众三千馀家，爲寇害。

translations.literal: Guan Cheng of Changguang county had follower households numbering over three thousand and wrought bandit harm.
translations.idiomatic: County leader Guan Cheng commanded three thousand families in raids.

sentences.zh: 议者欲举兵攻之。

translations.literal: Counselors wished to raise troops and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers urged a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 夔曰：“承等非生而乐乱也，习於乱，不能自还，未被德教，故不知反善。

translations.literal: Kui said, 'Cheng and the rest were not born delighting in turmoil; habituated to chaos they cannot return themselves; virtue's instruction has not reached them—therefore they do not know to turn toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: He Kui argued Guan Cheng's people learned violence from circumstance, not malice; lacking moral instruction they could still reform.

sentences.zh: 今兵迫之急，彼恐夷灭，必并力战。

translations.literal: Now if troops press them urgently they will fear extermination and surely unite their strength to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Coercion would make them fear annihilation and fight with desperate unity.

sentences.zh: 攻之既未易拔，虽胜，必伤吏民，不如徐喻以恩德，使容自悔，可不烦兵而定。”

translations.literal: Attacking will not be easy to overcome; even if victorious, clerks and commoners must be harmed—better gradually instruct them with kindness so they may contain themselves and repent; thus they may be settled without troubling the army.
translations.idiomatic: A siege would cost blood even in victory; patience and mercy could win surrender without battle.

sentences.zh: 乃遣郡丞黄珍往，爲陳成败，承等皆请服。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Assistant Governor Huang Zhen to explain success and failure; Cheng and the others all asked to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Huang Zhen with terms; Guan Cheng's band submitted.

sentences.zh: 夔遣吏成弘领校尉，长广县丞等郊迎奉牛酒，诣郡。

translations.literal: Kui sent Clerk Cheng Hong to lead them as colonel; the Changguang county assistants and others met him beyond the walls offering cattle and wine and proceeded to the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: He detailed Cheng Hong as colonel while county aides rode out with cattle and wine to escort the column to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 矣平贼从钱，众亦数千，夔率郡兵与張辽共讨定之。

translations.literal: In Jiaodong the bandit Cong Qian likewise had hosts numbering several thousand; Kui led commandery troops together with Zhang Liao and jointly pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Another coastal chieftain, Cong Qian, led thousands; He Kui joined Zhang Liao's column to crush them.

sentences.zh: 東牟人王营，众三千馀家，胁昌阳县爲乱。

translations.literal: Wang Ying of Dongmou had follower households over three thousand and coerced Changyang county into rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying of Dongmou rallied three thousand families and bullied Changyang into revolt.

sentences.zh: 夔遣吏王钦等，授以计略，使离散之。

translations.literal: Kui sent clerks Wang Qin and others, granting them stratagems to break them apart and scatter them.
translations.idiomatic: He Kui gave Wang Qin plans to split and dissolve the band.

sentences.zh: 旬月皆平定。

translations.literal: Within a month or so all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Inside a month quiet returned.

sentences.zh: 是时太祖始制新科下州郡，又收租税绵绢。

translations.literal: At this time the Grand Progenitor first instituted new statutes for commanderies and prefectures and likewise collected rent-tax in silk floss.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao rolled out fresh legal codes and silk levies across the provinces.

sentences.zh: 夔以郡初立，近以师旅之后，不可卒绳以法，乃上言曰：

translations.literal: Because the commandery had just been founded and lately emerged from campaigns, one could not instantly bind it with law; therefore he memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: He Kui argued the new prefecture needed breathing room after war and petitioned for gradual enforcement.

sentences.zh: 自丧乱已来，民人失所，今虽小安，然服教日浅。

translations.literal: Since turmoil and loss the people lost their homes; now though slightly settled, instruction has reached them only shallow days.
translations.idiomatic: The populace remained thinly accustomed to order after long wandering.

sentences.zh: 所下新科，皆以明罚敕法，齐一大化也。

translations.literal: The new statutes posted all clarify punishments and tidy law to unify great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The edicts aimed to unify behavior through clear penalties.

sentences.zh: 所领六县，疆域初定，加以饥馑，若一切齐以科禁，恐或有不从教者。

translations.literal: The six counties he leads—the territory has just been fixed and famine besides—if everything is clamped uniform by statute prohibitions, I fear some may refuse instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Six counties still hollow from famine might resist blanket statutes.

sentences.zh: 有不从教者不得不诛，则非观民设教随时之意也。

translations.literal: Those who refuse instruction cannot but be executed—then it is not the intent of observing the people and establishing instruction according to the hour.
translations.idiomatic: Mass executions for minor breaches would betray adaptive governance.

sentences.zh: 先王辨九服之赋以殊远近，制三典之刑以平治乱，愚以爲此郡宜依远域新邦之典，其民间小事，使长吏临时随宜，上不背正法，下以顺百姓之心。

translations.literal: Former kings distinguished the nine domains' levies to separate near and far; they framed three codes of punishments to balance order and chaos—I foolishly think this commandery ought to follow the canon for distant regions and new states; as for minor civilian affairs, let senior clerks respond provisionally as fits—above not betraying correct law, below complying with commoners' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings graded tribute by distance and matched punishments to chaos; He Kui asked leeway for remote Changguang until routine returned.

sentences.zh: 比及三年，民安其业，然后齐之以法，则无所不至矣。

translations.literal: Wait until three years when the people rest in their occupations—then align them with law—then nothing will remain beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: After three calm harvests, strict codes could apply everywhere.

sentences.zh: 太祖从其言。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao approved.

sentences.zh: 徵还，参丞相军事。

translations.literal: He was summoned back to serve as adviser on the chancellor's military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Recall brought him onto the chancellor's military council.

sentences.zh: 海贼郭祖寇暴乐安、济南界，州郡苦之。

translations.literal: Sea bandit Guo Zu raided viciously along the border of Le'an and Jinan; prefectures suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Pirate Guo Zu terrorized Le'an and Jinan until regional offices groaned.

sentences.zh: 太祖以夔前在长广有威信，拜乐安太守。

translations.literal: Because Kui previously at Changguang possessed awe-inspiring trustworthiness, he was appointed governor of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: He Kui's Changguang prestige won him the Le'an governorship.

sentences.zh: 到官数月，诸城悉平。

translations.literal: Several months after reaching office every walled town was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within months every citadel submitted.

sentences.zh: 入爲丞相東曹掾。

translations.literal: He entered service as aide in the chancellor's eastern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the eastern bureau under the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 夔言於太祖曰：

translations.literal: Kui spoke to the Grand Progenitor:
translations.idiomatic: He Kui advised Cao Cao:

sentences.zh: 自军兴以来，制度草创，用人未详其本，是以各引其类，时忘道德。

translations.literal: Since armies arose institutions were drafted in haste; employing men has not examined roots—therefore each faction pulls its own kind and sometimes forgets morality.
translations.idiomatic: Wartime staffing bred cliques that ignored virtue.

sentences.zh: 夔闻以贤制爵，则民慎德；

translations.literal: Kui has heard that when nobility is regulated by worth the people heed virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Merit-based ranks teach the people to cherish character.

sentences.zh: 以庸制禄，则民兴功。

translations.literal: when stipends are regulated by service the people rouse achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Service-based pay teaches them to strive.

sentences.zh: 以爲自今所用，必先核之鄉闾，使长幼顺叙，无相逾越。

translations.literal: Therefore those employed from now ought first be examined in village and hamlet so elder and junior keep proper order without leapfrogging one another.
translations.idiomatic: Nominees should win village scrutiny so seniority and merit stay aligned.

sentences.zh: 显忠直之赏，明公实之报，则贤不肖之分，居然别矣。

translations.literal: Display rewards for loyalty and bluntness, clarify response for solid merit—then worthy and unworthy divide themselves distinctly.
translations.idiomatic: Open rewards for candor and penalties for hollow fame would separate wheat from chaff.

sentences.zh: 又可脩保举故不以实之令，使有司别受其负。

translations.literal: One may also revise the ordinance on recommendation culpas when facts fail—make responsible offices separately bear the blame.
translations.idiomatic: False sponsors should face statutory blame.

sentences.zh: 在朝之臣，时受教与曹并选者，各任其责。

translations.literal: Court ministers who from time to time receive instruction and jointly select with the bureau should each bear their responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers who co-nominate must answer for their picks.

sentences.zh: 上以观朝臣之节，下以塞争竞之源，以督群下，以率万民，如是则天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Above it observes court ministers' integrity; below it plugs the spring of contention—thereby supervising officials and leading myriad commoners—if so the realm is greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Such rules would test integrity upstairs, choke patronage downstairs, and steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱善。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor praised this as good.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor praised this as good.

sentences.zh: 魏國既建，拜尚書僕射。

translations.literal: After the Wei state was established, He Kui was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei state was established, He Kui was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：時丁儀兄弟方进寵，儀與夔不合。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: At the time, Ding Yi and his brothers were just then advancing in favor, and Yi did not get along with Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Shu says: At the time, Ding Yi and his brothers were just then advancing in favor, and Yi did not get along with Kui.

sentences.zh: 尚書傅巽謂夔曰：『儀不相好已甚，子友毛玠，玠等儀已害之矣。子宜少下之！』

translations.literal: Secretariat official Fu Xun said to Kui, "Yi’s dislike of you has become extreme. Your friend Mao Jie and his companions have already been harmed by Yi. You should lower yourself to him a little!"
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat official Fu Xun said to Kui, "Yi’s dislike of you has become extreme. Your friend Mao Jie and his companions have already been harmed by Yi. You should lower yourself to him a little!"

sentences.zh: 夔曰：『爲不義適足害其身，焉能害人？且怀奸佞之心，立於明朝，其得久乎！』

translations.literal: Kui said, "Doing unrighteousness is only enough to harm oneself; how can it harm others? Besides, if one cherishes a treacherous and flattering heart while standing in an enlightened court, how can it last long!"
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "Doing unrighteousness is only enough to harm oneself; how can it harm others? Besides, if one cherishes a treacherous and flattering heart while standing in an enlightened court, how can it last long!"

sentences.zh: 夔終不屈志，儀后果以凶僞敗。

translations.literal: Kui never bent his resolve, and later Yi indeed fell through vicious falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Kui never bent his resolve, and later Yi indeed fell through vicious falsehood.

sentences.zh: 文帝爲太子，以凉茂爲太傅，夔爲少傅；特命二傅與尚書東曹並选太子諸侯官属。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was heir apparent, Liang Mao was made grand tutor and Kui junior tutor; by special order the two tutors and the eastern bureau of the Secretariat together selected officials and staff for the heir apparent and the princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was heir apparent, Liang Mao was made grand tutor and Kui junior tutor; by special order the two tutors and the eastern bureau of the Secretariat together selected officials and staff for the heir apparent and the princes.

sentences.zh: 茂卒，以夔代茂。

translations.literal: When Mao died, Kui replaced Mao.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao died, Kui replaced Mao.

sentences.zh: 每月朔，太傅入見太子，太子正法服而禮焉；他日無會儀。

translations.literal: On the first day of each month, the grand tutor entered to see the heir apparent, and the heir apparent put on formal ritual robes and treated him with ceremony; on other days there was no audience ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of each month, the grand tutor entered to see the heir apparent, and the heir apparent put on formal ritual robes and treated him with ceremony; on other days there was no audience ceremony.

sentences.zh: 夔遷太僕，太子欲與辭，宿戒供，夔無往意；乃與書请之，夔以國有常制，遂不往。

translations.literal: When Kui was promoted to grand coachman, the heir apparent wished to bid him farewell and had the supplies prepared the night before, but Kui had no intention of going; the heir then wrote to invite him, but Kui held that the state had fixed regulations, and so did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui was promoted to grand coachman, the heir apparent wished to bid him farewell and had the supplies prepared the night before, but Kui had no intention of going; the heir then wrote to invite him, but Kui held that the state had fixed regulations, and so did not go.

sentences.zh: 其履正如此。

translations.literal: Such was the way he walked in rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the way he walked in rectitude.

sentences.zh: 然於節儉之世，最爲豪汰。

translations.literal: Yet in an age that valued frugality, he was the most extravagant and wasteful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in an age that valued frugality, he was the most extravagant and wasteful.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，封成陽亭侯，邑三百户。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Kui was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengyang Pavilion, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Kui was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengyang Pavilion, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 疾病，屡乞遜位。

translations.literal: When he became ill, he repeatedly begged to yield his position.
translations.idiomatic: When he became ill, he repeatedly begged to yield his position.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：『蓋禮賢親舊，帝王之常务也。

translations.literal: The edict replied, "To honor worthies and be close to old associates is the constant duty of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied, "To honor worthies and be close to old associates is the constant duty of emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 以親則君有輔弼之勛焉，以賢則君有醇固之茂焉。

translations.literal: As an old associate, you have the merit of assistance and support; as a worthy, you have the excellence of pure solidity.
translations.idiomatic: As an old associate, you have the merit of assistance and support; as a worthy, you have the excellence of pure solidity.

sentences.zh: 夫有陰德者必有陽報，今君疾雖未瘳，神明聽之矣。

translations.literal: One who has hidden virtue must have manifest recompense. Now although your illness has not yet healed, the spirits have heard it.
translations.idiomatic: One who has hidden virtue must have manifest recompense. Now although your illness has not yet healed, the spirits have heard it.

sentences.zh: 君其即安，以順朕意。』

translations.literal: You should remain at ease, in accordance with my will."
translations.idiomatic: You should remain at ease, in accordance with my will."

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰靖侯。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his posthumous title was Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子 曾

translations.literal: Son: Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng, his heir.

sentences.zh: 子曾嗣，咸熙中爲司徒。

translations.literal: Son Zeng succeeded him; in the Xianxi era he became minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng inherited the line and rose to steward of education under Jin.

sentences.zh: 〈干宝《晋纪》曰：曾字颖考。

translations.literal: 〈Gan Bao's Jin ji records: Zeng, courtesy Yingkao.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Gan Bao's Jin annals gives his style as Yingkao.

sentences.zh: 正元中爲司隶校尉。

translations.literal: In the Zhengyuan years he was metropolitan commandant.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengyuan he served as metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 时毌丘俭孙女適刘氏，以孕系廷尉。

translations.literal: At the time the granddaughter of Wuqiu Jian by marriage to the Liu clan, being pregnant, was held by the minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqiu Jian's granddaughter, married into the Liu house while pregnant, sat in ministerial custody.

sentences.zh: 女母荀，爲武卫将军荀顗所表活，既免，辞诣廷尉，乞爲官婢以赎女命。

translations.literal: The girl's mother Xun was spared by petition of Guard-general Xun Yi; once freed she presented herself to the minister of justice begging to become a government bondmaid to ransom her daughter's life.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Xun, reprieved through Xun Yi, pleaded to enter penal service to save the girl.

sentences.zh: 曾使主簿程咸爲议，议曰：“大魏承奏、汉之弊，未及革制。

translations.literal: Zeng ordered chief clerk Cheng Xian to draft an opinion; the opinion stated: Great Wei inherits Qin and Han abuses without yet reforming institutions.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng had Cheng Xian argue that Wei still carried harsh Qin-Han precedent.

sentences.zh: 所以追戮已出之女，诚欲殄丑类之族也。

translations.literal: Therefore pursuing execution even on daughters already married away truly intends to exterminate ugly kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Executing married-out women aimed to extirpate rebel kin wholesale.

sentences.zh: 若已产育，则成他家之母。

translations.literal: If they have already borne children then they become mothers of other houses.
translations.idiomatic: Women who bore children belonged to their husbands' clans.

sentences.zh: 於防则不足惩奸乱之源，於情则伤孝子之思，男不御罪於他族，而女独婴戮於二门，非所以哀矜女弱，均法制之大分也。

translations.literal: As prevention it does not suffice to punish the font of treason; as sentiment it wounds filial sons' thoughts—men do not bear guilt in other lineages while women alone suffer execution in two gates—this is not how to pity weak women or balance the great divisions of law.
translations.idiomatic: The policy neither deterred crime nor spared grieving husbands—it punished women twice while men walked free.

sentences.zh: 臣以爲在室之女，可从父母之刑，既醮之妇，使从夫家之戮。”

translations.literal: Your servant thinks daughters still in the chamber may follow parents' punishment; wives already capped at marriage should follow husbands' households in execution.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed maidens answer for birth families, wives for marital houses.

sentences.zh: 朝廷从之，乃定律令。

translations.literal: The court followed it and thereupon fixed statute commands.
translations.idiomatic: The throne codified his distinction.

sentences.zh: 《晋诸公赞》曰：曾以高雅称，加性纯孝，位至太宰，封朗陵县公。

translations.literal: Jin zhu gong zan states: Zeng was famed for lofty refinement; moreover nature purely filial; he reached grand tutor, enfeoffed lord of Langling county.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin praise of ministers calls him refined and dutiful, ending as grand tutor and Langling duke.

sentences.zh: 年八十馀薨，谥曰元公。

translations.literal: Past eighty he died; posthumous title Lord Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died past eighty with posthumous name Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子邵嗣。

translations.literal: Son Shao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Son He Shao inherited.

sentences.zh: 邵字敬祖，才识深博，有经國体仪。

translations.literal: Shao, courtesy Jingzu, had talent and learning broad and deep, possessing the deportment that orders states.
translations.idiomatic: He Shao, style Jingzu, combined erudition with statesmanlike bearing.

sentences.zh: 位亦至太宰，谥康公。

translations.literal: Rank likewise reached grand tutor; posthumous title Lord Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He too became grand tutor as Lord Kang posthumously.

sentences.zh: 子蕤嗣。

translations.literal: Son Rui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Son He Rui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 邵庶兄遵，字思祖，有幹能。

translations.literal: Shao's elder half-brother by concubine Zun, courtesy Sizu, had administrative capability.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine-born elder brother He Zun, style Sizu, was an able administrator.

sentences.zh: 少經清職，終於太僕。

translations.literal: In youth he passed through pure offices and ended as minister of coaches.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through honorific posts to minister of coaches.

sentences.zh: 遵子绥，字伯蔚，亦以幹事称。

translations.literal: Zun's son Sui, courtesy Bowei, likewise was famed for administrative effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: He Zun's son He Sui, style Bowei, earned repute as a troubleshooter.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中爲尚書，爲司馬越所杀。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia era he was minister of the masters of writing and was killed by Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongjia he directed the masters of writing until Sima Yue executed him.

sentences.zh: 《傅子》称曾及荀顗曰：“以文王之道事其亲者，其颍昌何侯乎！

translations.literal: The Fu zi praises Zeng together with Xun Yi: Who serves kin with King Wen's path—the lord of Yingchang He?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan pairs He Zeng with Xun Yi as paragons of familial devotion.

sentences.zh: 其荀侯乎！

translations.literal: Or the lord Xun!
translations.idiomatic: Or Lord Xun!

sentences.zh: 古稱曾、闵，今曰荀、何。

translations.literal: Antiquity sang Zeng and Min; today one names Xun and He.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient lore praised Zeng Shen and Min Ziqian; Wei-Jin writers cited Xun and He.

sentences.zh: 内尽其心以事其親，外崇禮讓以接天下。

translations.literal: Within they exhaust heart to serve kin; without they honor yielding ritual to receive all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly filial, outwardly courteous to the world.

sentences.zh: 孝子，百世之宗；

translations.literal: Filial sons are ancestors for a hundred generations;
translations.idiomatic: Filial sons anchor lineages for ages.

sentences.zh: 仁人，天下之令也。

translations.literal: humane men are commanders for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Humane men become models for the empire.

sentences.zh: 有能行仁孝之道者，君子之仪表矣。”〉

translations.literal: Those able to practice humane filial ways are gentlemen's standards.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever embodies both sets the gentleman's measure.

sentences.zh: 邢颙字子昂，河间鄚人也。

translations.literal: Xing Yong, courtesy Ziang, was a man of Mo in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Yong, courtesy Ziang, hailed from Mo county in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 举孝廉，司徒辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: Recommended filial and incorrupt, summoned by the minister of education—both he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He refused filial-incorrupt nomination and ministerial summons alike.

sentences.zh: 易姓字，適右北平，从田畴游。

translations.literal: He changed surname and courtesy name, went to Right Beiping, and traveled with Tian Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Assuming an alias, he fled to Right Beiping and studied under Tian Chou.

sentences.zh: 积五年，而太祖定冀州。

translations.literal: Five years accumulated and the Grand Progenitor pacified Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later Cao Cao conquered Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 颙谓畴曰：“黄巾起来二十馀年，海内鼎沸，百姓流离。

translations.literal: Yong said to Chou: The Yellow Turbans arose over twenty years ago; within the seas cauldron boils; commoners drift and wander.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Yong told Tian Chou that decades of Turban chaos had scattered the people.

sentences.zh: 今闻曹公法令严。

translations.literal: Now I hear Lord Cao's commands and statutes are strict.
translations.idiomatic: He heard Cao Cao ruled with stern law.

sentences.zh: 民厌乱矣，乱极则平。

translations.literal: The people weary of chaos; chaos pushed to the limit turns to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Weary folk welcomed an end to turmoil.

sentences.zh: 请以身先。”

translations.literal: I ask to take my body first.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered to lead the way homeward.

sentences.zh: 遂装还鄉里。

translations.literal: Thereupon he packed and returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: He journeyed home.

sentences.zh: 田畴曰：“邢颙，民之先觉也。”

translations.literal: Tian Chou said: Xing Yong is the people's early awakener.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou called him the first to sense returning peace.

sentences.zh: 乃见太祖，求爲鄉导以克柳城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appeared before the Grand Progenitor and sought to be guide to overcome Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chou then sought Cao Cao out as guide against Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖辟颙爲冀州从事，时人称之曰：“德行堂堂邢子昂。”

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor summoned Yong as aide in Ji Province; people of the time styled him: Magnificent in virtue—Xing Ziang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao enlisted him for Ji staff; contemporaries sang of Magnificent Xing Ziang.

sentences.zh: 除广宗长，以故将丧弃官。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Guangzong; because an old commander died he abandoned office.
translations.idiomatic: Made Guangzong magistrate, he resigned mourning a former patron's death.

sentences.zh: 有司举正，太祖曰：“颙笃於旧君，有一致之节。”

translations.literal: Responsible offices impeached him; the Grand Progenitor said: Yong is earnest toward old lords—he possesses consistency of principle.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachers struck; Cao Cao praised his loyalty to past masters.

sentences.zh: 勿问也。

translations.literal: Do not question him.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade prosecution.

sentences.zh: 更辟司空掾，除行唐令，劝民农桑，风化大行。

translations.literal: Again summoned as aide to the minister of works, appointed acting magistrate of Xingtang—he urged the people in farming and mulberry; transforming influence spread greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Rehired under the ministry, he governed Xingtang, pushing silk and grain until custom flourished.

sentences.zh: 入爲丞相门下督，迁左冯翊，病，去官。

translations.literal: He entered as overseer of clients under the chancellor and advanced to junior guardian of the left; illness made him leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gate superintendent then left assistant governor of the capital before illness struck.

sentences.zh: 是时，太祖诸子高选官属，令曰：“侯家吏，宜得渊深法度如邢颙辈。”

translations.literal: At this time the Grand Progenitor's sons were choosing high officials for staff; an order said: Household clerks of marquises ought to obtain depth of law like men of Xing Yong's sort.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao ordered princes to hire jurists of Xing Yong's caliber.

sentences.zh: 遂以爲平原侯植家丞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made him household steward for Plain Marquis Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xing Yong became Cao Zhi's majordomo.

sentences.zh: 颙防闲以礼，无所屈挠，由是不合。

translations.literal: Yong barred excess with ritual and nowhere bent—therefore they did not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual discipline estranged him from the free-spirited prince.

sentences.zh: 庶子刘桢書谏植曰：“家丞邢颙，北土之彦，少秉高节，玄静澹泊，言少理多，真雅士也。

translations.literal: Secondary son Liu Zhen wrote remonstrating Zhi: Household steward Xing Yong is paragon of the northern soil—in youth holding lofty principle, silent and spare of words yet rich in sense—a true refined gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen urged Cao Zhi to honor Xing Yong's austere northern integrity.

sentences.zh: 桢诚不足同贯斯人，并列左右。

translations.literal: Zhen truly does not suffice to share rank with this man, standing side by side at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen admitted his own mediocrity beside Yong.

sentences.zh: 而桢礼遇殊特，颙反疏简，私惧观者将谓君侯习近不肖，礼贤不足，采庶子之春華，忘家丞之秋实。

translations.literal: Yet Zhen receives ritual treatment extraordinarily special while Yong on the contrary is kept distant and plain—I privately fear observers will say my lord is accustomed to drawing near the unworthy, insufficient in honoring worthies—plucking the secondary son's spring blossoms while forgetting the household steward's autumn fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cao Zhi lavished Liu Zhen and cold-shouldered Yong—onlookers might call him one who prized flashy companions over fruitful advisers.

sentences.zh: 爲上招谤，其罪不小，以此反侧。”

translations.literal: It invites slander above—the fault is not small—therefore I toss uneasily.
translations.idiomatic: Such imbalance courted scandal, Liu Zhen warned.

sentences.zh: 后参丞相军事，转東曹掾。

translations.literal: Later he joined the chancellor's military staff and shifted to aide in the eastern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Yong later served on military council and eastern bureau.

sentences.zh: 初，太子未定，而临菑侯植有宠，丁仪等并赞翼其美。

translations.literal: At first the heir was unsettled while Marquis Zhi of Linzi was favored; Ding Yi and others together praised and aided his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: While succession hung open, Ding Yi boosted Cao Zhi.

sentences.zh: 太祖问颙，颙对曰：“以庶代宗，先世之戒也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor asked Yong; Yong answered: Using the lesser branch to replace the trunk is warning from former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Asked by Cao Cao, Xing Yong cited the peril of elevating younger sons.

sentences.zh: 原殿下深重察之！”

translations.literal: I pray Your Highness reverently examine deeply!
translations.idiomatic: He begged the heir apparent to weigh the matter with utmost care.

sentences.zh: 太祖识其意，后遂以爲太子少傅，迁太傅。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor grasped his intent and afterward therefore made him junior tutor to the heir apparent and promoted him grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao heard him and later named him tutor to the crown prince, then senior tutor.

sentences.zh: 文帝践阼，爲侍中尚書仆射，赐爵关内侯，出爲司隶校尉，徙太常。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Xing Yong became palace attendant and vice director of the Secretariat, was granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes, went out as metropolitan commandant, and was transferred to minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Xing Yong became palace attendant and vice director of the Secretariat, was granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes, went out as metropolitan commandant, and was transferred to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 黄初四年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth Huangchu year.
translations.idiomatic: He died Huangchu 4.

sentences.zh: 子友嗣。

translations.literal: Son You succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xing You inherited.

sentences.zh: 〈晋诸公赞曰：颙曾孙乔，字曾伯。

translations.literal: 〈Jin zhu gong zan states: Yong's great-grandson Qiao, courtesy Zengbo.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Jin praise mentions descendant Xing Qiao, style Zengbo.

sentences.zh: 有体量局幹，美於当世。

translations.literal: He had capacity and measure, admired in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned poise and competence.

sentences.zh: 历清职。

translations.literal: He passed through pure offices.
translations.idiomatic: He served in honorific posts.

sentences.zh: 元康中，与刘涣俱爲尚書吏部郎，稍迁至司隶校尉。〉

translations.literal: In the Yuankang years together with Liu Huan he was ministerial clerk for personnel in the masters of writing and gradually rose to metropolitan commandant.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang saw him personnel clerk with Liu Huan, later metropolitan commandant.〉

sentences.zh: 鲍勋字叔业，泰山平阳人也，汉司隶校尉鲍宣九世孙。

translations.literal: Bao Xun, courtesy name Shuye, was from Pingyang in Taishan and was a ninth-generation descendant of Bao Xuan, metropolitan commandant under Han.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xun, courtesy name Shuye, was from Pingyang in Taishan and was a ninth-generation descendant of Bao Xuan, metropolitan commandant under Han.

sentences.zh: 宣后嗣有从上党徙泰山者，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Among Xuan's later descendants, some moved from Shangdang to Taishan, and so the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Among Xuan's later descendants, some moved from Shangdang to Taishan, and so the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 勋父信，灵帝时爲骑都尉，大将军何进遣东募兵。

translations.literal: Xun's father Xin served as commandant of cavalry under Emperor Ling, and Grand General He Jin sent him east to recruit troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's father Xin served as commandant of cavalry under Emperor Ling, and Grand General He Jin sent him east to recruit troops.

sentences.zh: 后爲济北相，协规太祖，身以遇害。

translations.literal: Later he became chancellor of Jibei, joined in planning with Grand Progenitor, and met death in person.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became chancellor of Jibei, joined in planning with Grand Progenitor, and met death in person.

sentences.zh: 语在《董卓传》、《武帝纪》。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the "Biography of Dong Zhuo" and the "Annals of Emperor Wu."
translations.idiomatic: The matter is recorded in the "Biography of Dong Zhuo" and the "Annals of Emperor Wu."

sentences.zh: 《魏书》曰：信父丹，官至少府侍中，世以儒雅显。

translations.literal: The Wei shu says: Xin's father Dan held office as chamberlain for revenues and palace attendant, and for generations the family was distinguished for cultivated refinement.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu says: Xin's father Dan held office as chamberlain for revenues and palace attendant, and for generations the family was distinguished for cultivated refinement.

sentences.zh: 少有大节，宽厚爱人，沈毅有谋。

translations.literal: From youth Xin had great integrity; he was generous, loved others, was calm and resolute, and had strategic judgment.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xin had great integrity; he was generous, loved others, was calm and resolute, and had strategic judgment.

sentences.zh: 大将军何进辟拜骑都尉，遣归募兵，得千馀人，还到成皋而进已遇害。

translations.literal: Grand General He Jin summoned and appointed him commandant of cavalry, then sent him home to recruit troops; he obtained more than a thousand men, but when he returned as far as Chenggao, Jin had already been killed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General He Jin summoned and appointed him commandant of cavalry, then sent him home to recruit troops; he obtained more than a thousand men, but when he returned as far as Chenggao, Jin had already been killed.

sentences.zh: 信至京师，董卓亦始到。

translations.literal: When Xin reached the capital, Dong Zhuo had also just arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin reached the capital, Dong Zhuo had also just arrived.

sentences.zh: 信知卓必爲乱，劝袁绍袭卓，绍畏卓不敢发。

translations.literal: Xin knew Zhuo would surely cause disorder and urged Yuan Shao to attack him, but Shao feared Zhuo and did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Xin knew Zhuo would surely cause disorder and urged Yuan Shao to attack him, but Shao feared Zhuo and did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 语在《绍传》。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the "Biography of Shao."
translations.idiomatic: The matter is recorded in the "Biography of Shao."

sentences.zh: 信乃引军还乡里，收徒众二万，骑七百，辎重五千馀乘。

translations.literal: Xin then led his army back to his home district and gathered twenty thousand followers, seven hundred cavalry, and more than five thousand wagons of baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then led his army back to his home district and gathered twenty thousand followers, seven hundred cavalry, and more than five thousand wagons of baggage.

sentences.zh: 是岁，太祖始起兵於己吾，信与弟韬以兵应太祖。
