translations.literal: That year, Grand Progenitor first raised troops at Jiwu, and Xin and his younger brother Tao responded to him with their troops.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Grand Progenitor first raised troops at Jiwu, and Xin and his younger brother Tao responded to him with their troops.

sentences.zh: 太祖与袁绍表信行破虏将军，韬裨将军。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor and Yuan Shao memorialized that Xin should act as general who breaks the caitiffs, and Tao as assistant general.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor and Yuan Shao memorialized that Xin should act as general who breaks the caitiffs, and Tao as assistant general.

sentences.zh: 时绍众最盛，豪杰多向之。

translations.literal: At the time Shao's following was the strongest, and many heroes inclined toward him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shao's following was the strongest, and many heroes inclined toward him.

sentences.zh: 信独谓太祖曰：『夫略不世出，能总英雄以拨乱反正者，君也。

translations.literal: Xin alone said to Grand Progenitor, "Strategy does not appear in every generation; the one who can unite the heroes, clear away disorder, and restore correctness is you.
translations.idiomatic: Xin alone said to Grand Progenitor, "Strategy does not appear in every generation; the one who can unite the heroes, clear away disorder, and restore correctness is you.

sentences.zh: 苟非其人，虽强必毙。

translations.literal: If a man is not the right person, even if he is strong, he must perish.
translations.idiomatic: If a man is not the right person, even if he is strong, he must perish.

sentences.zh: 君殆天之所启！』

translations.literal: You are almost certainly the one opened by Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: You are almost certainly the one opened by Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 遂深自结纳，太祖亦亲异焉。

translations.literal: He then bound himself closely to Grand Progenitor, and Grand Progenitor also treated him with special intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He then bound himself closely to Grand Progenitor, and Grand Progenitor also treated him with special intimacy.

sentences.zh: 汴水之败，信被疮，韬在陈战亡。

translations.literal: In the defeat at the Bian River, Xin was wounded, and Tao died in battle at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the defeat at the Bian River, Xin was wounded, and Tao died in battle at Chen.

sentences.zh: 绍劫夺韩馥位，遂据冀州。

translations.literal: Shao seized Han Fu's position by force and then occupied Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shao seized Han Fu's position by force and then occupied Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 信言於太祖曰：『奸臣乘衅，荡覆王室，英雄奋节，天下乡应者，义也。

translations.literal: Xin said to Grand Progenitor, "A treacherous minister took advantage of an opening and overturned the royal house; heroes roused their integrity, and all under Heaven responded because of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xin said to Grand Progenitor, "A treacherous minister took advantage of an opening and overturned the royal house; heroes roused their integrity, and all under Heaven responded because of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今绍爲盟主，因权专利，将自生乱，是复有一卓也。

translations.literal: Now Shao is alliance leader, and relying on authority he monopolizes advantage; he is about to generate disorder himself. This is to have another Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shao is alliance leader, and relying on authority he monopolizes advantage; he is about to generate disorder himself. This is to have another Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 若抑之，则力不能制，祗以遘难，又何能济？

translations.literal: If we try to restrain him, our strength cannot control him; we will only encounter disaster, so what can be accomplished?
translations.idiomatic: If we try to restrain him, our strength cannot control him; we will only encounter disaster, so what can be accomplished?

sentences.zh: 且可规大河之南，以待其变。』

translations.literal: For now we can plan for the region south of the Great River and wait for his change."
translations.idiomatic: For now we can plan for the region south of the Great River and wait for his change."

sentences.zh: 太祖善之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor approved this.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲东郡太守，表信爲济北相。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor became governor of Dong Commandery, he memorialized for Xin to become chancellor of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor became governor of Dong Commandery, he memorialized for Xin to become chancellor of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 会黄巾大众入州界，刘岱欲与战，信止之，岱不从，遂败。

translations.literal: When a large Yellow Turban force entered the province, Liu Dai wished to fight them; Xin tried to stop him, but Dai did not listen and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When a large Yellow Turban force entered the province, Liu Dai wished to fight them; Xin tried to stop him, but Dai did not listen and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 语在《武纪》。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the "Annals of Wu."
translations.idiomatic: The matter is recorded in the "Annals of Wu."

sentences.zh: 太祖以贼恃胜而骄，欲设奇兵挑击之於寿张。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor judged that the bandits, relying on victory, had become arrogant, and he wished to set an ambush and strike them at Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor judged that the bandits, relying on victory, had become arrogant, and he wished to set an ambush and strike them at Shouzhang.

sentences.zh: 先与信出行战地，后步军未至，而卒与贼遇，遂接战。

translations.literal: He first went out with Xin to inspect the battlefield, but before the infantry arrived, they suddenly encountered the bandits and joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: He first went out with Xin to inspect the battlefield, but before the infantry arrived, they suddenly encountered the bandits and joined battle.

sentences.zh: 信殊死战，以救太祖，太祖仅得溃围出，信遂没，时年四十一。

translations.literal: Xin fought desperately to save Grand Progenitor; Grand Progenitor only barely broke through the encirclement and escaped, and Xin was then lost, aged forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Xin fought desperately to save Grand Progenitor; Grand Progenitor only barely broke through the encirclement and escaped, and Xin was then lost, aged forty-one.

sentences.zh: 虽遭乱起兵，家本修儒，治身至俭，而厚养将士，居无馀财，士以此归之。

translations.literal: Although he encountered disorder and raised troops, his family had originally cultivated Confucian learning; he governed himself with utmost frugality, yet generously supported his officers and soldiers, kept no surplus wealth at home, and for this the soldiers turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Although he encountered disorder and raised troops, his family had originally cultivated Confucian learning; he governed himself with utmost frugality, yet generously supported his officers and soldiers, kept no surplus wealth at home, and for this the soldiers turned to him.

sentences.zh: 建安十七年，太祖追录信功，表封勋兄邵新都亭侯。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jian'an, Grand Progenitor posthumously recorded Xin's merit and memorialized to enfeoff Xun's elder brother Shao as Marquis of Xindu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Jian'an, Grand Progenitor posthumously recorded Xin's merit and memorialized to enfeoff Xun's elder brother Shao as Marquis of Xindu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 《魏书》曰：邵有父风，太祖嘉之，加拜骑都尉，使持节。

translations.literal: The Wei shu says: Shao had his father's manner, and Grand Progenitor admired him, additionally appointing him commandant of cavalry and granting him staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu says: Shao had his father's manner, and Grand Progenitor admired him, additionally appointing him commandant of cavalry and granting him staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 邵薨，子融嗣。

translations.literal: When Shao died, his son Rong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao died, his son Rong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 辟勋丞相掾。

translations.literal: Xun was summoned as an assistant in the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was summoned as an assistant in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 魏书曰：勋清白有高节，知名於世。

translations.literal: The Wei shu says: Xun was pure and upright and had lofty integrity, and he was known in his age.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu says: Xun was pure and upright and had lofty integrity, and he was known in his age.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，立太子，以勋爲中庶子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year they established the heir apparent and appointed Bao Xun as attendant of the household for the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was named in the twenty-second year, Bao Xun joined his household as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 徙黄门侍郎，出爲魏郡西部都尉。

translations.literal: Shifted to palace attendant under the yellow gates; went out as chief commandant of the western division of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to yellow-gate attendant and western Wei commandery chief commandant.

sentences.zh: 太子郭夫人弟爲曲周县吏，断盗官布，法应弃市。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Lady Guo's younger brother served as clerk of Quzhou county; he cut and stole government cloth—the law called for execution and exposure in the market.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's brother-in-law, a Quzhou clerk, stole official cloth—a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 太祖时在谯，太子留鄴，数手書爲之请罪。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Progenitor was at Qiao; the heir apparent stayed at Ye and repeatedly sent handwritten letters begging forgiveness on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was at Qiao while the crown prince stayed in Ye, sending repeated pleas to spare his brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 勋不敢擅纵，具列上。

translations.literal: Xun did not dare quietly release him but listed everything and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xun refused a quiet discharge and forwarded the full dossier to court.

sentences.zh: 勋前在東宫，守正不挠，太子固不能悦，及重此事，恚望滋甚。

translations.literal: Previously Xun had served in the eastern palace, guarding rectitude without bending—the heir had firmly been unable to delight in him; when this matter compounded it, resentment welled ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xun's stern tenure in the heir's household had already bitter Cao Pi; enforcing the law on Lady Guo's kin deepened the grudge.

sentences.zh: 会郡界休兵有失期者，密敕中尉奏免勋官。

translations.literal: It happened that soldiers missing assembly deadlines appeared in the commandery borders; he secretly ordered the capital commandant to memorialize stripping Xun of office.
translations.idiomatic: When troops missed muster in his jurisdiction, the prince secretly had the capital commandant impeach Bao Xun out of office.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜侍御史。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he received appointment as palace censor.

sentences.zh: 延康元年，太祖崩，太子即王位，勋以驸馬都尉兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yankang, Grand Progenitor died, the heir apparent assumed the royal throne, and Bao Xun, as commandant of the imperial son-in-law, concurrently served as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yankang, Grand Progenitor died, the heir apparent assumed the royal throne, and Bao Xun, as commandant of the imperial son-in-law, concurrently served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禅，勋每陳“今之所急，唯在军农，宽惠百姓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received abdication Xun often declared 'What is urgently needed now lies solely in army and agriculture—extend kindness to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: As emperor, Bao Xun kept urging priority for armies, farms, and mercy for the people.

sentences.zh: 台榭苑囿，宜以爲后。”

translations.literal: Terraced halls and hunting parks ought to come afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces and hunts could wait.

sentences.zh: 文帝将出游猎，勋停车上疏曰：“臣闻五帝三王，靡不明本立教，以孝治天下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was about to go out touring hunt Xun halted his carriage and submitted a memorial: 'Your servant has heard that none among the Five Emperors and Three Kings failed to clarify root and establish instruction, governing all under Heaven with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped Cao Pi's hunt with a tract on classical rulers founding rule on filial piety.

sentences.zh: 陛下仁圣恻隐，有同古烈。

translations.literal: Your Majesty humane and sage, compassionate—matching ancient exemplars.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Cao Pi's benevolence as worthy of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臣冀当继踪前代，令万世可则也。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes you will follow former dynastic footprints so myriad ages may take example.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor to leave a model for posterity.

sentences.zh: 如何在谅闇之中，修驰骋之事乎！

translations.literal: How may one amid mourning curtains cultivate galloping sport!
translations.idiomatic: How could mourning permit reckless riding?

sentences.zh: 臣冒死以闻，唯陛下察焉。”

translations.literal: Your servant risks death to bring this forward—only Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: He risked execution to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 帝手毁其表而竞行猎，中道顿息，问侍臣曰：“猎之爲乐，何如八音也？”

translations.literal: The emperor tore the memorial by hand yet competed to go hunting; midway he halted and asked attending ministers 'Compared with the eight tones, how is hunting's pleasure?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi shredded the memorial yet rode out, then mid-hunt asked whether sport beat music.

sentences.zh: 侍中刘晔对曰：“猎胜於乐。”

translations.literal: Attendant Liu Ye answered 'Hunting surpasses music.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye flattered him that hunting topped orchestral joy.

sentences.zh: 勋抗辞曰：“夫乐，上通神明，下和人理，隆治致化，万邦咸乂。

translations.literal: Xun replied bluntly 'Music ascends to communicate spirits and descends to harmonize human principle—it elevates governance and spreads transformation so myriad regions share peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xun countered that music linked heaven and earth and civilized the realm.

sentences.zh: 移风易俗，莫善於乐。

translations.literal: To shift customs and change habits nothing excels music.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Music says reforming manners begins with pitch and rhythm.

sentences.zh: 况猎，暴華盖於原野，伤生育之至理，栉风沐雨，不以时隙哉？

translations.literal: Moreover hunting exposes the splendid canopy in wilderness and wounds the supreme principle of nurturing life—combing wind and rinsing rain—does it seize proper intervals?
translations.idiomatic: Hunting battered nature and wasted seasons compared with harmonious sound.

sentences.zh: 昔鲁隐观渔於棠，春秋讥之。

translations.literal: Long ago Duke Yin of Lu watched fishing at Tang—the Spring and Autumn mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Duke Yin's infamous fishing junket.

sentences.zh: 虽陛下以爲务，愚臣所不原也。”

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty takes it as essential business, your foolish servant cannot approve.
translations.idiomatic: Even imperial enthusiasm could not sway him.

sentences.zh: 因奏：“刘晔佞谀不忠，阿顺陛下过戏之言。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized 'Liu Ye is flatteringly disloyal, parroting Your Majesty's playful words.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Liu Ye for toadying.

sentences.zh: 昔梁丘据取媚於遄台，晔之谓也。

translations.literal: Long ago Liang Qiu Ju curried favor at Swift Terrace—Ye is such a one.
translations.idiomatic: He compared Liu Ye to Qi court sycophants.

sentences.zh: 请有司议罪以清皇庙。”

translations.literal: I ask responsible offices debate guilt to cleanse the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded judicial review to purify the court.

sentences.zh: 帝怒作色，罢还，即出勋爲右中郎将。

translations.literal: The emperor flushed with rage, broke off, returned, and immediately sent Xun out as general of the household guards on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Cao Pi banished him to right household guard general.

sentences.zh: 黄初四年，尚書令陳群、仆射司馬宣王并举勋爲宫正，宫正即御史中丞也。

translations.literal: In the fourth Huangchu year Director of the masters of writing Chen Qun and vice director Prince Sima Yi together recommended Xun as palace rectifier—the palace rectifier is assistant imperial censor.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 4 saw Chen Qun and Sima Yi nominate Bao Xun as palace rectifier—equivalent to imperial censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已而用之，百寮严惮，罔不肃然。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice but to employ him; the hundred officials stood in stern awe—none failed to be solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Forced to agree, Cao Pi watched officials snap to discipline under Bao Xun.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，帝欲征吴，群臣大议，勋面谏曰：“王师屡征而未有所克者，盖以吴、蜀脣齿相依，凭阻山水，有难拔之势故也。

translations.literal: In autumn of the sixth year the emperor wished to campaign against Wu; great ministers debated broadly; Xun remonstrated face to face: 'Our king's army has repeatedly campaigned yet gained no victory—because Wu and Shu are lips and teeth protecting each other, relying on mountains and rivers—therefore they possess hard-to-uproot momentum.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that Wu's alliance with Shu and river barriers doomed repeat invasions.

sentences.zh: 往年龙舟飘荡，隔在南岸，圣躬蹈危，臣下破胆。

translations.literal: In former years the dragon boat drifted and bobbed, stranded on the southern shore—your sagely person trod danger and ministers below shattered their gall.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Cao Pi's boat stranded south of the Yangzi, terrifying the court.

sentences.zh: 此时宗庙几至倾覆，爲百世之戒。

translations.literal: At that time the ancestral temple nearly overturned—it becomes warning for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: That near disaster must caution future campaigns.

sentences.zh: 今又劳兵袭远，日费千金，中國虚耗，令黠虏玩威，臣窃以爲不可。”

translations.literal: Now again to weary troops striking far—daily expense of a thousand in gold—the central states hollow out while cunning barbarians sport with our might—your servant privately thinks it impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Another expedition would bleed the treasury while enemies mocked Wei strength.

sentences.zh: 帝益忿之，左迁勋爲治書执法。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier and demoted Xun to clerk-investigator of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Cao Pi cut him to archival clerk.

sentences.zh: 帝从壽春还，屯陳留郡界。

translations.literal: The emperor returned from Shouchun and encamped on the border of Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Shouchun, Cao Pi camped along Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 太守孙邕见，出过勋。

translations.literal: Governor Sun Yong paid audience; leaving he passed Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Sun Yong exited audience past Bao Xun's station.

sentences.zh: 时营垒未成，但立标埒，邕邪行不从正道，军营令史刘曜欲推之，勋以堑垒未成，解止不举。

translations.literal: At that time ramparts were unfinished—only boundary stakes stood; Yong walked askew not following the proper road; camp clerk Liu Yao wished to impeach him; Xun because trench lines were incomplete dismissed it and did not raise the case.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong shortcutted stakes; Liu Yao sought charges; Bao Xun withheld prosecution until fortifications stood.

sentences.zh: 大军还洛阳，曜有罪，勋奏绌遣，而曜密表勋私解邕事。

translations.literal: When the great army returned to Luoyang Yao committed an offense; Xun memorialized his dismissal and dispatch away—yet Yao secretly memorialized that Xun had privately excused Yong's affair.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Yao fell afoul; Bao Xun cashiered him, so Liu Yao snitched about Sun Yong.

sentences.zh: 诏曰：“勋指鹿作馬，收付廷尉。”

translations.literal: An edict stated 'Xun calls a deer a horse—seize him and hand to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict accused Bao Xun of twisting truth like Zhao Gao.

sentences.zh: 廷尉法议：“正刑五岁。”

translations.literal: The minister of justice's legal deliberation: 'Apply orthodox punishment five years.
translations.idiomatic: Judges proposed five years penal labor.

sentences.zh: 三官駮：“依律罚金二斤。”

translations.literal: The three offices objected 'According to statute fine two jin of metal.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewers argued for a copper fine only.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：“勋无活分，而汝等敢纵之！

translations.literal: The emperor raged greatly saying 'Xun has no portion of life—yet you dare indulge him!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi screamed that Bao Xun deserved death, not fines.

sentences.zh: 收三官已下付刺奸，当令十鼠同穴。”

translations.literal: Seize officials below the three offices and deliver to accusation investigators—let ten rats share one hole.
translations.idiomatic: He threatened to bury judges with informers like rats in a pit.

sentences.zh: 太尉锺繇、司徒華歆、镇军大将军陳群、侍中辛毗、尚書卫臻、守廷尉高柔等并表“勋父信有功於太祖”，求请勋罪。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zhong Yao, Minister of Education Hua Xin, General-in-Chief Chen Qun on campaign defense, palace attendant Xin Pi, minister Wei Zhen, acting minister of justice Gao Rou jointly memorialized 'Xun's father Xin had merit toward the Grand Progenitor' begging forgive Xun's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees cited Bao Xin's service to Cao Cao pleading mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝不许，遂诛勋。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit and thereupon executed Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi refused and executed Bao Xun.

sentences.zh: 勋内行既脩，廉而能施，死之日，家无馀财。

translations.literal: Xun's inner conduct was cultivated; incorrupt yet generous—on the day he died his household lacked surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He died poor despite private virtue.

sentences.zh: 后二旬，文帝亦崩，莫不爲勋叹恨。

translations.literal: Twenty days later Emperor Wen likewise died—none failed to sigh regret for Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Two weeks later Cao Pi died; observers mourned Bao Xun anew.

sentences.zh: 司馬芝

translations.literal: Sima Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Sima Zhi.

sentences.zh: 司馬芝字子華，河内温人也。

translations.literal: Sima Zhi, courtesy Zihua, was a man of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhi, courtesy Zihua, came from Wen county in Henei.

sentences.zh: 少爲書生，避乱荆州，於鲁阳山遇贼，同行者皆弃老弱走，芝独坐守老母。

translations.literal: In youth he was a scholar; fleeing turmoil to Jing Province he met bandits on Mount Luyang—traveling companions all abandoned the aged and weak and fled; Zhi alone sat guarding his old mother.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing to Jing, robbers cornered his party; companions fled, but he shielded his mother.

sentences.zh: 贼至，以刃临芝，芝叩头曰：“母老，唯在诸君！”

translations.literal: When bandits arrived they laid blades at Zhi; Zhi knocked his head saying 'Mother is aged—I leave her only to you gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: He begged brigands to spare his elderly mother.

sentences.zh: 贼曰：“此孝子也，杀之不义。”

translations.literal: The bandits said 'This is a filial son—to kill him lacks righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: They called him dutiful and stayed their swords.

sentences.zh: 遂得免害，以鹿车推载母。

translations.literal: Thereupon he escaped harm and used a deer cart to wheel-load his mother.
translations.idiomatic: They escaped; he pushed her in a handcart.

sentences.zh: 居南方十馀年，躬耕守节。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the south over ten years, personally farming and keeping integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He farmed honorably south of the Yangzi for a decade.

sentences.zh: 太祖平荆州，以芝爲菅长。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Jing Province he made Zhi magistrate of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao named him magistrate of Jian county after taking Jing.

sentences.zh: 时天下草创，多不奉法。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was freshly founded—many did not obey law.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei saw widespread legal laxity.

sentences.zh: 郡主簿刘节，旧族豪侠，宾客千馀家，出爲盗贼，入乱吏治。

translations.literal: Commandery chief clerk Liu Jie, old lineage heroic knight, had guest-followers over a thousand households—outward they became bandits, inward they disrupted clerical governance.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Liu Jie ran a thousand-client racket inside and outside the yamen.

sentences.zh: 顷之，芝差节客王同等爲兵，掾史据白：“节家前后未尝给繇，若至时藏匿，必爲留负。”

translations.literal: Shortly Zhi assigned Jie's guests Wang Tong and others as soldiers; clerks cited precedent saying 'Jie's household never supplied corvée—if time comes they will hide—surely leaving arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Staff warned Liu Jie's retainers would dodge conscription.

sentences.zh: 芝不听，与节書曰：“君爲大宗，加股肱郡，而宾客每不与役，既众庶怨望，或流声上闻。

translations.literal: Zhi did not listen, and wrote to Jie, "You are head of a great lineage and are attached to a commandery that is a limb of the state, yet your guests repeatedly do not take part in service; the common people already resent and complain, and perhaps rumor of it has reached above.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi did not listen, and wrote to Jie, "You are head of a great lineage and are attached to a commandery that is a limb of the state, yet your guests repeatedly do not take part in service; the common people already resent and complain, and perhaps rumor of it has reached above.

sentences.zh: 今

translations.literal: Now,
translations.idiomatic: Now,

translations.literal: having listed
translations.idiomatic: having listed

sentences.zh: 同等爲兵，幸时发遣。”

translations.literal: Tong and the others as soldiers, I hope you will dispatch them on time."
translations.idiomatic: Tong and the others as soldiers, I hope you will dispatch them on time."

sentences.zh: 兵已集郡，而节藏同等，因令督邮以军兴诡责县，县掾史穷困，乞代同行。

translations.literal: When troops had assembled at the commandery Jie hid Tong and peers; thereupon he ordered the postal inspector under military exigency falsely to blame the county—county clerks were desperate and begged to substitute going in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie hid the conscripts and pressured the county through bogus military orders.

sentences.zh: 芝乃驰檄济南，具陳节罪。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon flew a bulletin to Jinan laying out Jie's crimes in full.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhi reported Liu Jie to Jinan in writing.

sentences.zh: 太守郝光素敬信芝，即以节代同行，青州号芝“以郡主簿爲兵”。

translations.literal: Governor Hao Guang had always respected and trusted Zhi, and he therefore made Jie replace Tong and the others; Qing Province nicknamed Zhi "the man who made a commandery chief clerk into a soldier."
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hao Guang had always respected and trusted Zhi, and he therefore made Jie replace Tong and the others; Qing Province nicknamed Zhi "the man who made a commandery chief clerk into a soldier."

sentences.zh: 迁广平令。

translations.literal: He was promoted magistrate of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to Guangping magistrate.

sentences.zh: 征虏将军刘勋，贵宠骄豪，又芝故郡将，宾客子弟在界数犯法。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Captives Liu Xun, noble favorite arrogant and powerful, also Zhi's former commander—guest-followers and sons younger brothers within the border repeatedly violated law.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun's hangers-on broke laws in Sima Zhi's county.

sentences.zh: 勋与芝書，不著姓名，而多所属讬，芝不报其書，一皆如法。

translations.literal: Xun wrote Zhi without signing name yet entrusted much—Zhi did not answer his letter—everything followed statute.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhi ignored anonymous pull peddling and judged by code alone.

sentences.zh: 后勋以不轨诛，交关者皆获罪，而芝以见称。

translations.literal: Later Xun was executed for conspiracy—those connected all suffered punishment—yet Zhi was praised on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xun fell for treason, Sima Zhi won praise for incorruptibility.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：勋字子台，琅邪人。

translations.literal: 〈Wei lüe records: Xun courtesy Zitai, man of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Weilüe identifies Liu Xun as Zitai from Langye.

sentences.zh: 中平末，爲沛國建平长，与太祖有旧。

translations.literal: Late Zhongping era he was magistrate of Jianping in Pei state—had old ties with the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han he governed Jianping in Pei and knew Cao Cao of old.

sentences.zh: 后爲庐江太守，爲孙策所破，自归太祖，封列侯，遂从在散伍议中。

translations.literal: Later he was governor of Lujiang—broken by Sun Ce—submitted himself to the Grand Progenitor—enfeoffed full marquis—thereupon followed in miscellaneous counsels.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce smashed his Lujiang command; he surrendered to Cao Cao, took a column marquisate, and joined staff debates.

sentences.zh: 勛兄爲豫州刺史，病亡。

translations.literal: Xun's elder brother was governor of Yu Province—died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother died as Yu Province governor.

sentences.zh: 兄子威，又代从政。

translations.literal: The brother's son Wei likewise succeeded in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Liu Wei inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 勋自恃与太祖有宿，日骄慢，数犯法，又诽谤。

translations.literal: Xun relied on old ties with the Grand Progenitor—daily arrogant and lax—repeatedly violated law—also slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun presumed on Cao Cao's friendship, broke laws, and spread libel.

sentences.zh: 爲李申成所白，收治，并免威官。〉

translations.literal: Li Shengcheng informed on him—seized for punishment—and Wei too was stripped of office.〉
translations.idiomatic: Li Shengcheng denounced him; Liu Wei lost rank too.〉

sentences.zh: 迁大理正。

translations.literal: He was promoted rectifier of the minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to senior judge under the minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 有盗官练置都厕上者，吏疑女工，收以付狱。

translations.literal: Someone stole official silk and placed it on the capital privy—clerks suspected palace women workers—seized and handed to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Theft of palace silk implicated female artisans wrongly.

sentences.zh: 芝曰：“夫刑罪之失，失在苛暴。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "The failure in punishments and crimes lies in harsh violence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "The failure in punishments and crimes lies in harsh violence.

sentences.zh: 今赃物先得而后讯其辞，若不胜掠，或至诬服。

translations.literal: Now the stolen goods are first obtained and only afterward the statements are questioned; if a man cannot endure the beating, he may reach the point of making a false confession.
translations.idiomatic: Now the stolen goods are first obtained and only afterward the statements are questioned; if a man cannot endure the beating, he may reach the point of making a false confession.

sentences.zh: 诬服之情，不可以折狱。

translations.literal: The circumstances of a false confession cannot be used to decide a case.
translations.idiomatic: The circumstances of a false confession cannot be used to decide a case.

sentences.zh: 且简而易从，大人之化也。

translations.literal: Moreover, being simple and easy to follow is the transforming influence of a great man.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, being simple and easy to follow is the transforming influence of a great man.

sentences.zh: 不失有罪，庸世之治耳。

translations.literal: Not letting the guilty escape is only the governance of a mediocre age.
translations.idiomatic: Not letting the guilty escape is only the governance of a mediocre age.

sentences.zh: 今宥所疑，以隆易從之義，不亦可乎！』

translations.literal: Now to pardon what is doubtful, thereby elevating the meaning of being easy to follow, would that not be acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: Now to pardon what is doubtful, thereby elevating the meaning of being easy to follow, would that not be acceptable!"

sentences.zh: 太祖從其議。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor followed his deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 历甘陵、沛、陽平太守，所在有绩。

translations.literal: He passed through governor of Ganling, Pei, and Yangping—wherever stationed had achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Ganling, Pei, and Yangping with distinction.

sentences.zh: 黄初中，入爲河南尹，抑强扶弱，私请不行。

translations.literal: Mid Huangchu he entered as governor of Henan—suppressing strong and aiding weak—private pleas did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: As Henan governor he shielded the weak and barred pull.

sentences.zh: 会内官欲以事讬芝，不敢发言，因芝妻伯父董昭。

translations.literal: It happened palace personnel wished to entrust affairs to Zhi—did not dare speak openly—therefore went through Zhi's wife's uncle Dong Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs tried reaching him via Dong Zhao.

sentences.zh: 昭犹惮芝，不爲通。

translations.literal: Zhao still feared Zhi and did not relay it.
translations.idiomatic: Even Dong Zhao hesitated to ask.

sentences.zh: 芝爲教与群下曰：“盖君能设教，不能使吏必不犯也。

translations.literal: Zhi issued an instruction to his subordinates, saying, "A lord can establish instructions, but cannot make it certain that officials will never violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi issued an instruction to his subordinates, saying, "A lord can establish instructions, but cannot make it certain that officials will never violate them.

sentences.zh: 吏能犯教，而不能使君必不闻也。

translations.literal: Officials can violate the instructions, but cannot make it certain that the lord will never hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials can violate the instructions, but cannot make it certain that the lord will never hear of it.

sentences.zh: 夫设教而犯，君之劣也；

translations.literal: To establish instructions and have them violated is the lord's deficiency;
translations.idiomatic: To establish instructions and have them violated is the lord's deficiency;

sentences.zh: 犯教而闻，吏之祸也。

translations.literal: to violate instructions and have it heard of is the official's disaster.
translations.idiomatic: to violate instructions and have it heard of is the official's disaster.

sentences.zh: 君劣於上，吏祸於下，此政事所以不理也。

translations.literal: With the lord deficient above and officials meeting disaster below, this is why government affairs are not ordered.
translations.idiomatic: With the lord deficient above and officials meeting disaster below, this is why government affairs are not ordered.

sentences.zh: 可不各勉之哉！”

translations.literal: Can each of you fail to exert himself!"
translations.idiomatic: Can each of you fail to exert himself!"

sentences.zh: 於是下吏莫不自励。

translations.literal: Thereupon lower clerks none failed to spur themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Staff tightened discipline overnight.

sentences.zh: 门下循行尝疑门幹盗簪，幹辞不符，曹执爲狱。

translations.literal: A gate attendant once suspected a gate clerk of stealing a hairpin—the clerk's words did not match—the bureau seized him for prison.
translations.idiomatic: A patrolman accused a gate runner of pin theft on thin grounds.

sentences.zh: 芝教曰：“凡物有相似而难分者，自非离娄，鲜能不惑。

translations.literal: Zhi instructed them, saying, "Whenever things resemble one another and are difficult to distinguish, unless one is Li Lou, few can avoid being confused.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi instructed them, saying, "Whenever things resemble one another and are difficult to distinguish, unless one is Li Lou, few can avoid being confused.

sentences.zh: 就其实然，循行何忍重惜一簪，轻伤同类乎！

translations.literal: If the true situation is considered, how could a patrolman bear to value one hairpin so heavily and lightly injure one of his own kind!
translations.idiomatic: If the true situation is considered, how could a patrolman bear to value one hairpin so heavily and lightly injure one of his own kind!

sentences.zh: 其寝勿问。”

translations.literal: Let the matter rest and do not inquire into it."
translations.idiomatic: Let the matter rest and do not inquire into it."

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，赐爵关内侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, Sima Zhi was granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, Sima Zhi was granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 顷之，特进曹洪乳母当，与临汾公主侍者共事无涧神。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, Dang, the wet nurse of the special advance official Cao Hong, together with an attendant of Princess Linfen, served the spirit of Wujian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, Dang, the wet nurse of the special advance official Cao Hong, together with an attendant of Princess Linfen, served the spirit of Wujian.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：无涧，山名，在洛阳东北。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: Wujian is the name of a mountain, northeast of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Songzhi notes: Wujian is the name of a mountain, northeast of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 系狱。

translations.literal: They were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: They were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 卞太后遣黄门诣府传令，芝不通，辄敕洛阳狱考竟，而上疏曰：

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Bian sent a yellow-gate attendant to the office to transmit her command, but Zhi did not let it through; he immediately ordered the Luoyang prison to complete the investigation, and sent up a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bian sent a yellow-gate attendant to the office to transmit her command, but Zhi did not let it through; he immediately ordered the Luoyang prison to complete the investigation, and sent up a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 诸应死罪者，皆当先表须报。

translations.literal: All who should suffer capital crime must first memorialize awaiting reply.
translations.idiomatic: Death sentences required imperial confirmation.

sentences.zh: 前制書禁绝淫祀以正风俗，今当等所犯妖刑，辞語始定，黄门吴达诣臣，傳太皇太后令。

translations.literal: Former codified edicts forbade excessive sacrifice to rectify customs—now those such as Dang await sorcery punishment—their testimony just settled—yellow-gate Wu Da came to your servant transmitting Grand Empress Dowager's order.
translations.idiomatic: Prior bans on illicit cults framed Dang's sorcery trial when a eunuch relayed the empress dowager's command mid-case.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢通，惧有救护，速闻圣听，若不得已，以垂宿留。

translations.literal: Your servant dares not relay it, fearing rescue efforts would hasten word to the sagely listener—if unavoidable, allow it to linger overnight.
translations.idiomatic: He would not pass the message along lest protectors alert the emperor prematurely; only if compelled would he let the case sit overnight.

sentences.zh: 由事不早竟，是臣之罪，是以冒犯常科，辄敕县考竟，擅行刑戮，伏须诛罚。

translations.literal: Because the affair was not concluded early—this is your servant's crime—therefore offending ordinary precedent I ordered the county to conclude examination, presumptuously carrying out execution; I prostrate awaiting capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed to rushing a capital sentence without higher approval and offered himself for punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝手报曰：“省表，明卿至心，欲奉诏書，以权行事，是也。

translations.literal: The emperor replied in his own hand, "I have read your memorial and understand your utmost sincerity. You wished to honor the imperial edict and act according to practical authority; this was correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied in his own hand, "I have read your memorial and understand your utmost sincerity. You wished to honor the imperial edict and act according to practical authority; this was correct.

sentences.zh: 此乃卿奉诏之意，何谢之有？

translations.literal: This was precisely your intent in honoring the edict; what is there to apologize for?
translations.idiomatic: This was precisely your intent in honoring the edict; what is there to apologize for?

sentences.zh: 后黄门复往，慎勿通也。”

translations.literal: If yellow-gate attendants come again later, be careful not to let them through."
translations.idiomatic: If yellow-gate attendants come again later, be careful not to let them through."

sentences.zh: 芝居官十一年，数议科条所不便者。

translations.literal: Zhi held office eleven years, repeatedly debating statutes that proved inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: For eleven years as Henan governor he contested cumbersome laws.

sentences.zh: 其在公卿间，直道而行。

translations.literal: Among dukes and ministers he walked the straight path.
translations.idiomatic: Among high ministers he kept an uncompromising course.

sentences.zh: 会诸王来朝，与京都人交通，坐免。

translations.literal: It happened when various kings came to court and trafficked with capital residents—he sat guilty and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Princes' illicit contacts with Luoyang locals cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 后爲大司农。

translations.literal: Later he became minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He later directed the ministry of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 先是诸典农各部吏民，末作治生，以要利入。

translations.literal: Previously various agricultural colony officers—clerks and commoners—pursued secondary crafts for livelihood to chase profit income.
translations.idiomatic: Colony officials had turned tenant farmers toward trade sidelines.

sentences.zh: 芝奏曰：

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhi submitted:

sentences.zh: 王者之治，崇本抑末，务农重谷。

translations.literal: Royal governance esteems root and restrains branch—emphasize farming and treasure grain.
translations.idiomatic: The throne must privilege agriculture over commerce.

sentences.zh: 王制：‘无三年之储，國非其國也。

translations.literal: Royal regulation states: Without three years' stores the state is not a state.
translations.idiomatic: The royal ordinances demand three years' grain reserves.

sentences.zh: ’管子区言以积谷爲急。

translations.literal: Guanzi in terse sayings takes storing grain as urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong called granaries the first imperative.

sentences.zh: 方今二虏未灭，师旅不息，國家之要，惟在谷帛。

translations.literal: Now the two foes are not extinguished; armies do not rest—the state's essentials lie solely in grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Until Wu and Shu fell, grain and cloth remained the strategic priority.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝特开屯田之官，专以农桑爲业。

translations.literal: Martial Emperor specially opened agricultural colony offices dedicating them to farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao founded the colony system for tillage and silk alone.

sentences.zh: 建安中，天下仓廪充实，百姓殷足。

translations.literal: Mid Jian'an era granaries under Heaven were full; commoners were ample.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an granaries once overflowed and the people prospered.

sentences.zh: 自黄初以来，听诸典农治生，各爲部下之计，诚非國家大体所宜也。

translations.literal: Since Huangchu allowing various colony officers to pursue livelihood each calculating for their subordinates truly does not suit the great body of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu permissiveness let colonies chase private gain—a poor fit for national policy.

sentences.zh: 夫王者以海内爲家，故傳曰：‘百姓不足，君谁与足！

translations.literal: The king takes all within the seas as household—therefore the tradition says: If commoners are insufficient, with whom is the lord sufficient!
translations.idiomatic: The ruler shares one purse with the realm—Analects warn that broke peasants mean a broke throne.

sentences.zh: ’富足之田，在於不失天时而尽地力。

translations.literal: The field of abundance lies in not missing heaven's seasons and exhausting earth's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth comes from timely sowing and full use of soil.

sentences.zh: 今商旅所求，虽有加倍之显利，然於一统之计，已有不赀之损，不如垦田益一亩之收也。

translations.literal: Now what merchants seek though having doubled manifest profit yet toward unified planning already has immeasurable loss—not equal to reclaiming fields and increasing yield by one mu.
translations.idiomatic: Trading windfalls drain the strategic economy worse than opening one extra mu.

sentences.zh: 夫农民之事田，自正月耕种，耘锄条桑，耕熯种麦，穫刈筑场，十月乃毕。

translations.literal: Farmers' field work—from first month planting, weeding, pruning mulberry, plowing dry fields sowing wheat, harvest cutting building threshing floor—tenth month only finishes.
translations.idiomatic: The farming calendar runs solid labor from spring sowing through autumn threshing.

sentences.zh: 治廪系桥，运输租赋，除道理梁，墐涂室屋，以是终岁，无日不爲农事也。

translations.literal: Managing granaries tying bridges, transporting rent taxes, clearing roads repairing bridges, plastering walls thatching roofs—with this the whole year ends—no day not devoted to agricultural tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers spend the year hauling tax grain, mending roads, and patching roofs—no idle day.

sentences.zh: 今诸典农，各言‘留者爲行者宗田计，课其力，势不得不尔。

translations.literal: Now various colony officers each say: Those staying calculate traveling men's ancestral fields, assessing their labor—circumstances force it.
translations.idiomatic: Colony heads excuse sideline labor as tallying absentees' plots.

sentences.zh: 不有所废，则当素有馀力。

translations.literal: If nothing is abandoned then ordinarily there should be surplus strength.
translations.idiomatic: Without commercial distraction farmers would have spare effort.

sentences.zh: ’臣愚以爲不宜复以商事杂乱，专以农桑爲务，於國计爲便。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant thinks one ought not again mix commercial affairs in confusion—dedicate solely to farming and sericulture—convenient for state planning.
translations.idiomatic: He urged banning colony commerce to refocus on grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 明帝从之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 每上官有所召问，常先见掾史，爲断其意故，教其所以答塞之状，皆如所度。

translations.literal: Whenever superiors summoned with questions he always first met clerks, explaining their intent for them, teaching how to answer and satisfy—everything matched his estimates.
translations.idiomatic: He coached subordinates before imperial audiences until replies landed exactly as predicted.

sentences.zh: 芝性亮直，不矜廉隅。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature bright and straight—did not flaunt integrity's corners.
translations.idiomatic: He was candid without theatrical righteousness.

sentences.zh: 与宾客谈論，有不可意，便面折其短，退无异言。

translations.literal: Discussing with guests—when something displeased him he immediately rebuked their faults face to face—withdrawing he spoke no different words.
translations.idiomatic: He criticized companions openly and never gossiped behind their backs.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，家无馀财，自魏迄今爲河南尹者莫及芝。

translations.literal: He died in office; household lacked surplus wealth—from Wei until now none who were Henan governors matched Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died poor in post; later Henan governors were measured against him and found wanting.

sentences.zh: 子 岐

translations.literal: Son: Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Sima Qi.

sentences.zh: 芝亡，子岐嗣，从河南丞转廷尉正，迁陳留相。

translations.literal: When Zhi died son Qi succeeded—from Henan assistant shifted to rectifier of minister of justice, promoted minister of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qi inherited, rose from Henan aide to judge, then Chenliu minister.

sentences.zh: 梁郡有系囚，多所连及，数岁不决。

translations.literal: Liang commandery held bound prisoners many connected—several years unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Liang commandery jailed mass defendants for years unresolved.

sentences.zh: 诏書徙狱于岐属县，县请豫治牢具。

translations.literal: Edict moved prison to counties under Qi's jurisdiction—county requested beforehand to prepare jail gear.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transferred the case to his counties, which begged to build new cells.

sentences.zh: 岐曰：“今囚有数十，既巧诈难符，且已倦楚毒，其情易见。

translations.literal: Qi said: Now prisoners number several tens—already crafty fraud hard to match—and moreover already weary of Chu torture—their circumstances easy to see.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qi argued dozens of broken suspects could hide nothing more.

sentences.zh: 岂当复久处囹圄邪！”

translations.literal: How should they again long dwell in prison!
translations.idiomatic: Why prolong their jail time?

sentences.zh: 及囚室，诘之，皆莫敢匿诈，一朝决竟，遂超爲廷尉。

translations.literal: When reaching prisoner chambers and questioning them—none dared hide fraud—in one morning concluded—thereupon super-promoted to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Morning interrogations cleared every charge and vaulted him to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 是时大将军爽专权，尚書何晏、邓飏等爲之辅翼。

translations.literal: At that time General-in-Chief Shuang monopolized power; ministers He Yan and Deng Yang assisted him as wings.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang dominated court with He Yan and Deng Yang as allies.

sentences.zh: 南阳圭泰尝以言迕指，考系廷尉。

translations.literal: Gui Tai of Nanyang once spoke contrary to intent—examined and bound at minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Tai of Nanyang crossed power-holders and landed in jail.

sentences.zh: 飏讯狱，将致泰重刑。

translations.literal: Yang examined the prison—intended to impose heavy punishment on Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang meant to crush Gui Tai in trial.

sentences.zh: 岐数飏曰：“夫枢机大臣，王室之佐，既不能辅化成德，齐美古人，而乃肆其私忿，枉論无辜。

translations.literal: Qi repeatedly told Yang: Pivot ministers assisting the royal house—unable to aid transformation into virtue or match ancient beauty—yet vent private resentment and twist judgment on the guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qi rebuked Deng Yang for persecuting innocents while claiming to serve the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 使百姓危心，非此焉在？”

translations.literal: Making commoners stand in peril—if not here then where?
translations.idiomatic: Such cruelty was how rulers lost popular trust.

sentences.zh: 飏於是惭怒而退。

translations.literal: Yang thereupon ashamed and angry withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang stalked off humiliated and furious.

sentences.zh: 岐終恐久獲罪，以疾去官。

translations.literal: Qi ultimately feared long incurring guilt—used illness to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing reprisal, Sima Qi resigned on health grounds.

sentences.zh: 居家未期而卒，年三十五。

translations.literal: At home not one full year then died—age thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died within the year at thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 子肇嗣。

translations.literal: Son Zhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Son Sima Zhao inherited.

sentences.zh: 〈肇，晋太康中爲冀州刺史、尚書，见

translations.literal: 〈Zhao—in the Jin Taikang era served as Ji Province governor and minister of the masters of writing; see
translations.idiomatic: 〈During the Jin Taikang era he governed Ji Province and served as minister of the masters of writing; see

sentences.zh: （百官志）

translations.literal: (Treatise on the Hundred Offices)
translations.idiomatic: (Treatise on the Hundred Offices)

sentences.zh: 百官名。〉

translations.literal: and Register of Official Titles).〉
translations.idiomatic: and the Register of Official Titles).〉

sentences.zh: 作者評論

translations.literal: Author's appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary of the historian.

sentences.zh: 评曰：徐奕、何夔、邢颙贵尚峻厉，爲世名人。

translations.literal: Appraisal says: Xu Yi, He Kui, and Xing Yong esteemed severity and austerity—became famed men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou ranks Xu Yi, He Kui, and Xing Yong among the era's stern exemplars.

sentences.zh: 毛玠清公素履，司馬芝忠亮不倾，庶乎不吐刚茹柔。

translations.literal: Mao Jie was pure and fair in plain conduct; Sima Zhi loyal and bright without leaning—perhaps they did not swallow softness while spitting hardness.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jie and Sima Zhi embodied the classic refusal to truckle to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 崔琰高格最优，鮑勋秉正无亏，而皆不免其身，惜哉！

translations.literal: Cui Yan highest in lofty standard; Bao Xun upheld rectitude without flaw—yet none escaped harm to their persons—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan and Bao Xun stood tallest yet paid with their lives—a bitter loss.

sentences.zh: 大雅贵“既明且哲”，虞書尚“直而能温”，自非兼才，畴克备诸！

translations.literal: The Great Odes prizes both perspicacious and wise; the Documents esteems straight yet able to be mild—unless possessing combined talents who can fulfill them all!
translations.idiomatic: The canon demands both wisdom and warmth—few mortals unite every virtue.
